tasks.title: Establish Code Quality Standards and Fix Linting Issues
tasks.description: Address all existing `go vet` errors, install and configure `golangci-lint`, and establish a baseline for code quality to ensure project maintainability and stability before adding new features.
tasks.details: 1. Install `golangci-lint`: `go install github.com/golangci/golangci-lint/cmd/golangci-lint@latest`. 2. Create a `.golangci.yml` configuration file in the project root. Enable linters such as `govet`, `errcheck`, `staticcheck`, `unused`, and `typecheck`. 3. Run `golangci-lint run ./...` and methodically fix all reported issues. This includes fixing logger type mismatches, undefined constants, and incorrect test imports as mentioned in the PRD. 4. Integrate this check into the CI/CD pipeline to prevent future issues.
tasks.testStrategy: Verify that `go vet ./...` and `golangci-lint run ./...` commands complete successfully with zero errors. Code reviews should enforce adherence to the new linting rules. The CI pipeline must fail if any linting errors are introduced.

tasks.title: Complete Core Infrastructure: Logging, Configuration, and Migrations
tasks.description: Finalize the core infrastructure components, including implementing a proper logging configuration, completing the database migration system, and fixing configuration validation to ensure a stable and observable application foundation.
tasks.details: 1. **Logging**: Integrate a structured logging library like `zerolog` or `slog`. Configure log levels (debug, info, error) to be controllable via the YAML configuration file. Ensure all services and handlers use the structured logger. 2. **Configuration**: Implement struct tags for validation (e.g., using `github.com/go-playground/validator`) on the configuration struct to ensure all required fields are present and valid on startup. 3. **Database Migrations**: Use a library like `golang-migrate/migrate` to manage SQLite schema changes. Create initial migration files for all existing models and ensure the application runs migrations on startup.
tasks.testStrategy: Unit tests for configuration loading and validation should fail with invalid configs and pass with valid ones. Manually verify that changing the log level in the config file affects the application's log output. Test the migration system by starting with a fresh database and verifying the schema is created correctly.

tasks.title: Implement Pi Agent gRPC Client and System Monitoring
tasks.description: Develop the core functionality of the Pi Agent, enabling it to communicate with the central controller via gRPC and collect essential system metrics like CPU, memory, and temperature.
tasks.details: 1. **gRPC Client**: Implement the client-side logic for the gRPC services defined in the protobufs. The client should establish a secure TLS connection to the controller. Implement connection retry logic with exponential backoff. 2. **System Monitoring**: Use a library like `gopsutil` (`github.com/shirou/gopsutil`) to collect system metrics. Create a background goroutine that periodically collects CPU usage, memory usage, and system temperature and sends this data to the controller via a gRPC stream.
tasks.testStrategy: Create integration tests where a mock gRPC server receives data from the agent. Verify that the agent can connect, authenticate, and stream metrics. Unit test the metric collection functions to ensure they correctly parse system data.

tasks.title: Implement Real GPIO Hardware Control in Pi Agent
tasks.description: Integrate a hardware access library to provide real GPIO pin control (digital I/O, PWM) and support for I2C/SPI interfaces, replacing all placeholder functionality in the Pi Agent.
tasks.details: 1. **Hardware Library**: Integrate `periph.io/x/periph` for hardware abstraction. Initialize the library on agent startup using `host.Init()`. 2. **GPIO Control**: Implement the gRPC service handlers that map incoming requests to `periph.io` functions. For digital control, use `gpio.PinIO.Out()` and `gpio.PinIO.High/Low()`. For PWM, use the `pwm` package to set frequency and duty cycle. 3. **Hardware Detection**: Implement a startup routine to detect available hardware capabilities and report them to the controller upon registration.
tasks.testStrategy: This requires testing on actual Raspberry Pi hardware. Create a test suite that can be run on a Pi to toggle specific GPIO pins and verify the voltage change with a multimeter. For PWM, use an oscilloscope or LED brightness to verify output. Unit tests should mock the `periph.io` interfaces to test the gRPC handler logic without hardware.

tasks.title: Implement mDNS Discovery and Node Registration
tasks.description: Replace the mock mDNS implementation with a real one to allow the controller to automatically discover Pi agents on the network and manage their registration into the cluster.
tasks.details: 1. **mDNS Implementation**: Use the `hashicorp/mdns` library. The Pi Agent will act as an mDNS server, announcing a specific service type (e.g., `_pi-controller-agent._tcp`). The controller will run an mDNS client to browse for this service. 2. **Node Registration**: When the controller discovers a new agent, it should initiate a registration workflow. The agent provides its capabilities and requests to join the cluster. The controller validates the request, generates necessary credentials (see Task 75), and persists the new node in the database.
tasks.testStrategy: Set up a local network with a controller and multiple agent instances (can be on different machines or containers). Verify that the controller successfully discovers all agents within 30 seconds. Test that agents that leave the network are eventually marked as offline. Verify that newly discovered nodes appear in the database after registration.

tasks.title: Implement Secure Certificate Management and Node Authentication
tasks.description: Establish a secure communication channel between the controller and agents by implementing a certificate management system for node identity and authentication, enforcing TLS for all gRPC and API communication.
tasks.details: 1. **CA Setup**: The controller will act as a Certificate Authority (CA). On first startup, it should generate a root CA certificate and key if they don't exist. 2. **Certificate Issuance**: During the node registration process (from Task 74), the controller will generate a client certificate, sign it with its CA, and securely transmit it to the new agent. 3. **TLS Enforcement**: Configure the gRPC server (controller) and clients (agents) to use TLS, requiring mutual authentication (mTLS). The controller's API server (Gin) should also be configured to use TLS.
tasks.testStrategy: Integration tests should verify that agents without a valid, signed certificate are rejected by the controller. Test the certificate generation and signing logic. Use tools like `openssl s_client` to inspect the TLS configuration of the servers and verify the certificate chain.

tasks.title: Enhance Controller's GPIO Service for Real Hardware Communication
tasks.description: Remove all mock implementations in the controller's GPIO service and replace them with logic that communicates with the Pi agents via gRPC to perform actual hardware operations.
tasks.details: 1. **Remove Mocks**: Delete all placeholder code in the GPIO service layer that simulates hardware actions. 2. **gRPC Client Integration**: The GPIO service will now act as a gRPC client. When a user requests a GPIO action via the REST API, the service will look up the target node, establish a gRPC connection to the corresponding agent, and forward the request. 3. **State Management**: Implement GPIO state persistence in the database. When a pin is set, its state should be recorded. Add safety checks to prevent resource conflicts (e.g., two requests trying to control the same pin).
tasks.testStrategy: E2E Test: Use an HTTP client (like `curl` or Postman) to send a request to the controller's REST API to toggle a GPIO pin. Verify that the request is proxied through the gRPC connection to the agent and that the physical pin's state changes on the Raspberry Pi.

tasks.title: Implement K3s Provisioner Engine via SSH
tasks.description: Build the provisioning engine capable of installing K3s on a registered node. This involves implementing a secure SSH client, creating installation scripts, and managing the cluster bootstrapping process.
tasks.details: 1. **SSH Client**: Use the `golang.org/x/crypto/ssh` package to create a robust SSH client service. The service should manage connections using key-based authentication (keys can be provisioned during node registration). 2. **Provisioning Logic**: The provisioner service will expose an API endpoint to trigger a K3s installation on a specific node. The logic will SSH into the target node, execute a script to download and install K3s, and configure it as either a master or a worker node. 3. **Cluster State**: Store the cluster bootstrap token and node roles in the database to manage the lifecycle, including adding or removing nodes.
tasks.testStrategy: Test against virtual machines or Docker containers running an SSH server to simulate Raspberry Pi nodes. Verify that the provisioner can connect, execute commands, and transfer files. An E2E test would involve provisioning a multi-node K3s cluster and verifying its health using `kubectl`.

tasks.title: Define and Implement Kubernetes Custom Resource Definitions (CRDs)
tasks.description: Create the Kubernetes CRDs for managing hardware resources like `GPIOPin`, `PWMController`, and `I2CDevice`. This lays the groundwork for Kubernetes-native GPIO control.
tasks.details: 1. **CRD Schema**: Define the YAML schemas for each CRD. For a `GPIOPin`, this would include fields like `spec.pinNumber`, `spec.direction` (in/out), and `status.state` (high/low). Use the `kubebuilder` or `Operator SDK` toolkits to bootstrap the CRD files and associated Go types. 2. **Validation**: Implement OpenAPI v3 schema validation within the CRD definitions to enforce constraints (e.g., pin numbers must be within a valid range). 3. **Deployment**: Package the CRDs into the controller's deployment manifest so they are automatically applied to a Kubernetes cluster where the controller is running.
tasks.testStrategy: Unit test the Go type definitions. Integration tests using a real or test Kubernetes cluster (like `kind` or `k3d`) should apply the CRD manifests and verify that they are created successfully using `kubectl get crds`. Test creating instances of the custom resources and ensure validation rules are enforced.

tasks.title: Develop Kubernetes Controller for GPIO Custom Resources
tasks.description: Implement the reconciliation logic for the GPIO-related CRDs. The controller will watch for changes to these custom resources and translate them into actions via the Pi Controller's GPIO service.
tasks.details: 1. **Controller Logic**: Using `go.k8s.io/client-go`, implement a controller (operator pattern). This controller will set up informers to watch for Create, Update, and Delete events on the `GPIOPin` and other custom resources. 2. **Reconciliation Loop**: The core of the controller is the `Reconcile` function. When a `GPIOPin` resource is created or updated, this function will be triggered. It will read the spec, determine the target node, and call the Pi Controller's internal GPIO service (which in turn calls the agent via gRPC) to set the physical pin's state. 3. **Status Updates**: After performing the action, the controller must update the `status` subresource of the custom resource to reflect the actual state of the hardware.
tasks.testStrategy: Write integration tests for the controller using a test Kubernetes environment. Create a `GPIOPin` resource and verify that the controller attempts to call a mocked GPIO service. An E2E test would involve deploying the controller to a K3s cluster (provisioned in Task 77) and creating a CRD instance, then verifying the physical pin state changes on the target Pi.

tasks.title: Clean up Stale 'pi-agent' Binary References
tasks.description: Remove all references to the now-defunct 'pi-agent' binary from documentation, CI/CD workflows, and Docker configurations to align with the new single-binary architecture.
tasks.details:
The project has evolved from a two-binary system ('pi-controller' and 'pi-agent') to a single-binary architecture where 'pi-controller' serves both roles using subcommands (e.g., 'server' and 'agent'). This task involves removing all obsolete artifacts related to the old 'pi-agent' binary.

1.  **CI/CD Workflow Cleanup (.github/workflows):**
    *   Modify the release workflow (likely `.github/workflows/release.yml`) to remove any build and packaging steps specifically for `pi-agent`.
    *   Ensure the build matrix and asset upload steps only target and publish the single `pi-controller` binary for all supported architectures.

2.  **Docker Configuration Update (docker/):**
    *   Delete any Dockerfile specific to the agent (e.g., `docker/Dockerfile.agent`).
    *   Review the primary Dockerfile (`docker/Dockerfile`) to ensure it correctly builds the single binary.
    *   Update the `CMD` or `ENTRYPOINT` to reflect the subcommand usage, for example `CMD ["/usr/local/bin/pi-controller", "server"]`.
    *   If a separate image is needed for nodes, consider creating a new `Dockerfile.node` that uses the same binary but with a different command, like `CMD ["/usr/local/bin/pi-controller", "agent"]`.

3.  **Documentation Update (docs/):**
    *   Update `README.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, and any getting-started guides.
    *   Replace all mentions of running a separate `pi-agent` binary with the new `pi-controller agent ...` command.
    *   Update architecture diagrams and component descriptions to reflect the single-binary model.

4.  **Source Code and Build Scripts:**
    *   Delete the `cmd/pi-agent/` directory entirely, as its `main` package is now redundant.
    *   Inspect the root `Makefile` and remove any build, run, or clean targets related to `pi-agent`.
tasks.testStrategy:
1.  **CI/CD Verification:** Manually trigger the modified release workflow on a feature branch. Verify that the pipeline completes successfully and that the resulting release artifacts on GitHub contain only the `pi-controller` binary.
2.  **Docker Image Build:** Build the Docker image(s) locally using the updated Dockerfile(s). Run the container and use `docker ps` and `docker logs` to confirm it starts correctly with the new subcommand (e.g., `pi-controller server`).
3.  **Documentation Review:** Perform a full read-through of the updated documentation. Follow the setup and usage instructions from the perspective of a new user to ensure they are accurate and easy to understand.
4.  **Local Build Test:** Run `make clean` and `make build` (or equivalent commands) locally to confirm that only the `pi-controller` binary is built and no errors related to the missing `pi-agent` path occur.

tasks.title: Harden Internal Agent gRPC Communication with mTLS
tasks.description: Implement mutual TLS (mTLS) authentication for the agent gRPC server (port 9091) to secure communication between Pi agents and the controller, replacing the current insecure connection with certificate-based authentication.
tasks.testStrategy:
## Unit Tests

1. **Agent Server TLS Configuration Tests** (`internal/agent/server_test.go`):
   - Test server creation with valid TLS certificates
   - Test server creation with invalid certificates (should fail)
   - Test server creation without TLS (insecure mode)
   - Test server creation with missing CA file

2. **Agent Client Manager Tests** (`internal/grpc/client/pi_agent_client_test.go`):
   - Test client creation with mTLS enabled
   - Test client creation in insecure mode
   - Test TLS handshake failure scenarios
   - Test certificate validation

3. **Configuration Tests** (`internal/config/config_test.go`):
   - Test `AgentServerConfig.IsTLSEnabled()` method
   - Test loading configuration with agent TLS settings
   - Test validation of TLS certificate paths

## Integration Tests

1. **mTLS Connection Test** (`test/integration/agent_mtls_test.go`):
   ```go
   // Test establishing mTLS connection between controller and agent
   // 1. Generate test CA and certificates
   // 2. Start agent server with mTLS
   // 3. Create controller client with valid client certificate
   // 4. Verify successful connection and GPIO operation
   // 5. Attempt connection with invalid certificate (should fail)
   ```

2. **Certificate Verification Test**:
   - Verify that clients with invalid certificates are rejected
   - Verify that expired certificates are rejected
   - Verify that self-signed certificates without CA are rejected

3. **Backward Compatibility Test**:
   - Verify insecure mode still works (with appropriate warnings)
   - Verify mixed environments handle TLS/non-TLS gracefully

## Security Tests

1. **Security Test** (`test/security/agent_mtls_security_test.go`):
   - Test connection rejection without client certificate
   - Test connection rejection with wrong CA
   - Test connection rejection with expired certificate
   - Test man-in-the-middle protection
   - Verify TLS version enforcement (minimum TLS 1.2)
   - Verify cipher suite restrictions

## End-to-End Tests

1. **E2E mTLS GPIO Test**:
   - Deploy controller with mTLS configuration
   - Register agent node with proper certificates
   - Execute GPIO operation through Kubernetes CRD
   - Verify operation succeeds over mTLS connection
   - Monitor logs for mTLS handshake success

2. **Certificate Rotation Test**:
   - Issue initial certificates
   - Establish connection
   - Rotate certificates (issue new ones)
   - Verify connection continues working with new certificates

## Manual Verification

1. Use `openssl s_client` to verify agent server TLS configuration:
   ```bash
   openssl s_client -connect <agent-ip>:9091 -cert client.crt -key client.key -CAfile ca.crt
   ```

2. Check logs for mTLS initialization messages:
   - "Agent gRPC server configured with mutual TLS (mTLS)"
   - "Using mTLS for agent connection"

3. Verify certificate details match expected CN and SANs:
   ```bash
   openssl x509 -in agent-server.crt -text -noout
   ```

4. Test connection failure scenarios:
   - Remove client certificate → connection should fail
   - Use wrong CA → connection should fail
   - Use expired certificate → connection should fail

tasks.title: Configure SonarQube Project and sonar-project.properties File
tasks.description: Set up the SonarQube project in the 'yorkserv' organization and create the `sonar-project.properties` file in the project root to define scan parameters, exclusions, and coverage report paths.
tasks.details: Create the SonarQube project via the SonarCloud UI under the 'yorkserv' organization. Generate a new analysis token and store it as a `SONAR_TOKEN` secret in the GitHub repository settings. Also store the organization key as `SONAR_ORGANIZATION`. Create the `sonar-project.properties` file in the project root with the exact content specified in the PRD, ensuring `sonar.projectKey`, `sonar.organization`, `sonar.sources`, and other properties are correctly defined.
tasks.testStrategy: Verify that the `sonar-project.properties` file exists in the root directory and contains the correct configuration. Confirm that the `SONAR_TOKEN` and `SONAR_ORGANIZATION` secrets are created in the GitHub repository's 'Secrets and variables' > 'Actions' settings.

tasks.title: Implement SonarQube Scan GitHub Actions Workflow
tasks.description: Create the `.github/workflows/sonarqube.yml` workflow to automatically scan the codebase on pushes and pull requests to the `develop` and `main` branches.
tasks.details: Create a new workflow file at `.github/workflows/sonarqube.yml`. The workflow should trigger on push and pull_request events for the specified branches. It will use `actions/checkout@v4` and `actions/setup-go@v5` with Go version `1.21`. The key steps are running tests with coverage using `go test -v -coverprofile=coverage.out ./...` and then executing the scan with `sonar-scanner`. The recommended action is `sonarsource/sonarcloud-github-action@v2.2.0`, which simplifies the process. The action should be configured with the `SONAR_TOKEN` from GitHub secrets.
tasks.testStrategy: Create a pull request to the `develop` branch. Verify the 'SonarCloud Code Analysis' action is triggered and completes successfully. Check the workflow logs for any errors during the test execution or scan phase.

tasks.title: Configure SonarQube Quality Gates and PR Decoration
tasks.description: Define and apply the custom quality gate with specified thresholds for coverage, duplication, and code ratings. Enable pull request decoration for inline feedback.
tasks.details: In the SonarCloud UI for the `pi-controller` project, navigate to 'Quality Gates'. Create a new gate or copy the 'Sonar way' and add the custom conditions: 'Coverage on New Code' >= 80%, 'Duplicated Lines on New Code' <= 3%, 'Maintainability Rating on New Code' is better than A, 'Reliability Rating on New Code' is better than A, and 'Security Rating on New Code' is better than A. Assign this quality gate to the project. Ensure the SonarCloud GitHub App is installed and configured for the repository to enable PR decoration.
tasks.testStrategy: On the test pull request from the previous task, verify that the SonarQube status check appears. Confirm that it shows the quality gate status (pass/fail) and that code smells or coverage issues are reported as inline comments within the PR's 'Files changed' view.

tasks.title: Initialize Playwright Configuration and Directory Structure
tasks.description: Set up the initial `playwright.config.ts` in `web/kubes-aura`, create the test directory structure (`tests/setup`, `tests/utils`, `tests/e2e`), and add test scripts to `package.json`.
tasks.details: In the `web/kubes-aura` directory, run `npm install --save-dev @playwright/test@1.44.0`. Create the `playwright.config.ts` file and populate it with the configuration from the PRD, including `fullyParallel: true`, multiple reporters, `webServer` configuration, and trace settings. Create the directories: `tests/`, `tests/setup/`, `tests/utils/`, and `tests/e2e/`. Create empty placeholder files like `tests/setup/fixtures.ts`. Finally, update the `scripts` section of `web/kubes-aura/package.json` with the `test`, `test:ui`, `test:headed`, etc. commands.
tasks.testStrategy: Run `npm run test` from the `web/kubes-aura` directory. Expect it to fail if no tests exist, but the command should execute without configuration errors. Verify that the directory structure and new `package.json` scripts are present.

tasks.title: Implement Mock Data and Global Setup/Teardown
tasks.description: Create comprehensive mock data for nodes, clusters, and users in `test-data.ts` and implement global setup/teardown scripts to manage the test environment.
tasks.details: Populate `web/kubes-aura/tests/setup/test-data.ts` with the TypeScript interfaces and mock data arrays (`mockNodes`, `mockClusters`) as specified in the PRD. For the mock API, use a library like Mock Service Worker (`msw`). Create `web/kubes-aura/tests/setup/global-setup.ts` to define and start the mock API handlers before tests run. `global-teardown.ts` will stop the mock server. Update `playwright.config.ts` to point to these files: `globalSetup: require.resolve('./tests/setup/global-setup')`, `globalTeardown: require.resolve('./tests/setup/global-teardown')`.
tasks.testStrategy: Add a temporary test that makes a `fetch` request to a mocked endpoint (e.g., `/api/nodes`). Verify that the test receives the mocked data from `test-data.ts` and not a 404 or real API response.

tasks.title: Develop Playwright Test Helpers and Utilities
tasks.description: Create a set of reusable helper functions in `web/kubes-aura/tests/utils/helpers.ts` to streamline test writing for common actions like login, navigation, and assertions.
tasks.details: Implement the functions outlined in the PRD within `web/kubes-aura/tests/utils/helpers.ts`. For example, `export async function login(page: Page, user: string, pass: string) { ... }` will navigate to the login page, fill credentials, click submit, and wait for the dashboard URL. The `waitForApiResponse` function can be implemented using `page.waitForResponse('**/api/endpoint')`. This centralizes common logic.
tasks.testStrategy: Write unit tests for the helper functions where possible. For UI-interactive helpers like `login`, create a small, isolated test spec that calls the helper and asserts its outcome (e.g., the URL has changed to the dashboard).

tasks.title: Implement Custom Playwright Test Fixtures
tasks.description: Create custom test fixtures in `web/kubes-aura/tests/setup/fixtures.ts` to provide pre-configured, authenticated page objects and mock data directly to tests.
tasks.details: In `web/kubes-aura/tests/setup/fixtures.ts`, extend the base Playwright test object as shown in the PRD. The `authenticatedPage` fixture will use the `login` helper from `helpers.ts` to perform a login before the test begins, returning the authenticated `Page` object. Other fixtures like `mockNodes` can simply import the data from `test-data.ts` and provide it to the test context. This abstracts setup logic away from test files.
tasks.testStrategy: Create a simple test file that uses the `authenticatedPage` fixture. Add a `console.log(await page.url())` inside the test to verify that the URL is the post-login dashboard URL, proving the fixture successfully authenticated before the test body executed.

tasks.title: Create GitHub Actions Workflow for Playwright Tests
tasks.description: Implement the `.github/workflows/playwright.yml` workflow to automatically install dependencies, browsers, and run the Playwright test suite.
tasks.details: Create the workflow file `.github/workflows/playwright.yml` as defined in the PRD. Use `actions/checkout@v4` and `actions/setup-node@v4` with Node.js version 20. Ensure `working-directory: web/kubes-aura` is set for all npm/npx commands. The key steps are `npm ci`, `npx playwright install --with-deps`, `npm run test`, and `actions/upload-artifact@v4`. The `if: always()` condition on the upload step ensures reports are saved even if tests fail.
tasks.testStrategy: Commit and push the new workflow file on a pull request. Verify that the 'Playwright Tests' action triggers, installs all dependencies, and runs the tests. Check that the 'playwright-report' artifact is successfully uploaded and can be downloaded from the workflow run summary page.

tasks.title: Write Initial E2E Test to Validate Infrastructure
tasks.description: Create a sample end-to-end test that logs in and verifies the dashboard, ensuring the entire Playwright infrastructure (fixtures, mocks, helpers) is working correctly.
tasks.details: Create a new test file, `web/kubes-aura/tests/e2e/dashboard.spec.ts`. Write a test case using the custom fixtures, for example: `test('should display nodes on the dashboard', async ({ authenticatedPage, mockNodes }) => { ... });`. Inside the test, use locators to find elements on the page that should display data from the `mockNodes` fixture. For instance, `await expect(page.getByText(mockNodes[0].hostname)).toBeVisible();`. This test validates the full E2E testing loop.
tasks.testStrategy: Run the new test locally using `npm run test`. It should pass. Then, commit the test and verify that it passes in the CI environment as part of the `playwright.yml` workflow. This confirms the setup is stable and consistent across environments.

tasks.title: Document Testing and Code Quality Processes
tasks.description: Update the project's README files with sections detailing how to run tests locally, interpret SonarQube results, and troubleshoot common testing issues.
tasks.details: Edit the root `README.md` to add a 'Code Quality' section explaining the SonarQube integration and the meaning of a failed quality gate. Edit `web/kubes-aura/README.md` to add a 'Running Tests' section that lists and explains the new npm scripts (`test`, `test:ui`, `test:report`). Include a brief guide on how to add new mock data and create new tests using the established fixtures and helpers.
tasks.testStrategy: Ask a team member unfamiliar with the new setup to follow the documentation to run tests locally. They should be able to successfully execute the tests and view the report without further assistance. Review the documentation for clarity and completeness.

tasks.title: Setup Authentication Test Environment and Mock Data
tasks.description: Create the necessary test setup files, including mock user data and any specific Playwright fixtures required for authentication testing.
tasks.details: Create the file `web/kubes-aura/tests/setup/test-data.ts`. Populate it with the `mockUsers` object as specified in the PRD, including valid, admin, and expired session user data. Review the existing Playwright configuration (`playwright.config.ts`) to ensure the base URL and test directories are correctly configured. Create a basic fixture file `web/kubes-aura/tests/setup/fixtures.ts` if it doesn't exist, extending the base `test` from `@playwright/test`. Initially, this file can just export the extended test object.
tasks.testStrategy: Verify that `test-data.ts` is created and exports the `mockUsers` object correctly. Ensure the test suite can be run (even with no tests) without configuration errors. Import `mockUsers` into a test file and log the data to confirm it's accessible.

tasks.title: Implement Basic Login Flow Tests
tasks.description: Create the `auth.spec.ts` file and implement tests for displaying the login page and handling a successful login with valid credentials.
tasks.details: Create `web/kubes-aura/tests/e2e/auth.spec.ts`. Use the structure from the PRD with nested `describe` blocks. Implement the 'should display login page correctly' and 'should login successfully with valid credentials' tests. Use `mockUsers.validUser` from the test data file. Use Playwright's web-first assertions and resilient locators, e.g., `page.getByRole('heading', { name: 'Login' })` and `page.getByLabel('Username')`. The test should navigate to `/auth/login`, fill the form, submit, and assert the URL changes to `/pi-controller` and a logged-in indicator like `[data-testid="user-menu"]` is visible.
tasks.testStrategy: Run the tests using `npx playwright test auth.spec.ts`. The test for displaying the page should pass if the page loads. The successful login test should pass if it correctly fills credentials, submits, redirects to the dashboard, and the user menu is visible. The test should fail if any of these steps fail.

tasks.title: Implement Invalid Login and Form Validation Tests
tasks.description: Add tests to verify error handling for invalid credentials and client-side validation for empty form fields on the login page.
tasks.details: In `auth.spec.ts`, implement the 'should show error for invalid credentials' and 'should validate empty form fields' tests. For invalid credentials, use hardcoded incorrect data, submit the form, and assert that the URL remains `/auth/login` and an error message (`.error-message`) containing 'Invalid credentials' is visible. For empty fields, click the submit button without filling the form and use `expect(page.getByLabel('Username')).toBeInvalid()` to check for HTML5 validation attributes.
tasks.testStrategy: The invalid credentials test should verify that the user is not redirected and that a specific error message is displayed. The form validation test should confirm that submitting an empty form triggers browser-level validation messages and prevents form submission.

tasks.title: Implement 'Remember Me' and Session Persistence Test
tasks.description: Test the 'Remember Me' functionality to ensure the session persists across browser restarts by inspecting session cookies.
tasks.details: Implement the 'should persist session with Remember Me' test. This test will require using the `context` fixture provided by Playwright. The flow is: navigate to login, fill credentials, check the 'Remember Me' checkbox (`page.getByLabel('Remember Me')`), submit. After login, use `await context.cookies()` to get all browser cookies. Find the session cookie and assert its `expires` property is set to a future date (e.g., more than 7 days from now). Then, close the page, open a new page with `await context.newPage()`, navigate directly to a protected route (`/pi-controller`), and assert that the user is still logged in.
tasks.testStrategy: Run the test. It should successfully log in, find a session cookie with a long expiry date, and successfully access a protected route in a new page within the same browser context without needing to log in again.

tasks.title: Implement Successful Registration and Basic Validation
tasks.description: Implement tests for the user registration flow, including the happy path for successful registration and basic field validations.
tasks.details: In `auth.spec.ts`, under the 'Registration Flow' describe block, implement 'should display registration form correctly' and 'should register new user successfully'. For the successful registration, generate a unique username or email for each test run to avoid conflicts (e.g., `testuser-${Date.now()}@example.com`). Fill all fields with valid data, submit, and assert that the user is redirected to the login page. Also, add a test for email format validation.
tasks.testStrategy: The successful registration test will pass if a new user can be created and the page redirects to login. The email validation test should input an invalid email, attempt submission, and verify that a client-side or server-side validation error is displayed.

tasks.title: Implement Advanced Registration Validation Tests
tasks.description: Add tests to validate password strength requirements and the prevention of duplicate username or email registrations.
tasks.details: Implement the 'should validate password strength' and 'should prevent duplicate usernames' tests. For password strength, follow the PRD example: enter a weak password and assert that a specific error message (e.g., in `.password-error`) is displayed. For duplicate prevention, first register a user, then attempt to register a second user with the same username or email and assert that a 'Username already exists' or similar error is shown.
tasks.testStrategy: The password strength test passes if submitting with a weak password fails and shows the correct error. The duplicate user test passes if the second registration attempt is blocked and an appropriate error message is displayed on the page.

tasks.title: Implement Session Timeout and Logout Tests
tasks.description: Verify that user sessions expire after a configured timeout and that the logout functionality correctly terminates the session.
tasks.details: Implement 'should expire session after timeout' and 'should logout and clear session'. For logout, the test should log in, click the user menu, click the logout button, and assert redirection to the login page. It should also verify the session cookie is cleared using `context.cookies()`. For timeout, the test needs to simulate time passing. Since frontend cannot control server session time, this test may require a special test hook or API endpoint to invalidate the session. If not possible, simulate it as per the PRD by manipulating browser state (`localStorage`, etc.) and then attempting navigation, expecting a redirect to login.
tasks.testStrategy: The logout test passes if the user is redirected to login and the session cookie is gone. The session timeout test passes if, after the timeout period, an attempt to access a protected route redirects the user to the login page, preferably with a 'Session expired' message.

tasks.title: Implement Protected Route Access Test
tasks.description: Test that an unauthenticated user attempting to access a protected route is redirected to the login page.
tasks.details: In the 'Session Management' block, implement the 'should redirect to login when accessing protected route' test. This is a simple test that starts with a clean browser context (no logged-in user). The test should navigate directly to a known protected URL, such as `/pi-controller` or `/pi-controller/nodes`. It should then assert that the final URL is the login page's URL (`/auth/login`).
tasks.testStrategy: The test passes if the `page.goto('/pi-controller')` call results in `expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/auth\/login/)` being true. This confirms the server-side or middleware routing correctly handles unauthenticated requests.

tasks.title: Implement Security Tests for SQL Injection and XSS
tasks.description: Add security-focused tests to ensure the login and registration forms are not vulnerable to common SQL injection or Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) attacks.
tasks.details: Under the 'Security Validation' describe block, implement 'should prevent SQL injection in login form' and 'should sanitize XSS attempts'. For SQLi, use a common payload like `' OR '1'='1` in both username and password fields and assert that login fails and an 'Invalid credentials' error is shown. For XSS, use a payload like `<script>alert('xss')</script>` in a registration form field. The test must listen for dialog events (`page.on('dialog',...)`) and fail if one appears. The primary assertion is that the registration fails or the input is sanitized, and no script is executed.
tasks.testStrategy: The SQLi test passes if the malicious input does not result in a successful login. The XSS test passes if no JavaScript alert/dialog is triggered after submitting the form containing the script payload.

tasks.title: Implement Brute Force / Rate Limiting Test
tasks.description: Create a test to verify that the server enforces rate limiting on failed login attempts to prevent brute-force attacks.
tasks.details: Implement the 'should rate limit failed login attempts' test. This will involve creating a loop that attempts to log in with invalid credentials multiple times (e.g., 5-10 times). After a certain number of failed attempts, the test should assert that a new error message appears, such as 'Too many failed attempts. Please try again later.' or that subsequent requests are visibly slower or blocked (e.g., check for a 429 'Too Many Requests' response using `page.waitForResponse`).
tasks.testStrategy: The test passes if, after a defined number of consecutive failed logins, the UI displays a rate-limiting error message or the server responds with a 429 status code. This confirms the brute-force protection mechanism is active.

tasks.title: Setup Playwright Test Files and Mock Data
tasks.description: Create the necessary test spec files (`dashboard.spec.ts`, `navigation.spec.ts`) and a centralized module for mock data to be used across all dashboard and navigation tests.
tasks.details:
Create a file `tests/data/dashboard-mock-data.ts`. This file will export mock objects for nodes and clusters. Use `page.route()` in a `test.beforeEach` block to intercept API calls (e.g., `/api/nodes`, `/api/clusters`) and respond with this mock data. This ensures tests are deterministic and independent of backend state. Ensure `playwright.config.ts` is configured to use the existing authentication state from 'Task 2.1'.

Pseudo-code for `dashboard-mock-data.ts`:
`export const mockNodes = [{ id: 'node-1', name: 'pi-master', cpu: 75, temp: 60, ... }];`
`export const mockClusters = [{ id: 'cluster-1', name: 'Primary Cluster', nodeCount: 3, ... }];`

Pseudo-code for test setup:
`import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';`
`import { mockNodes, mockClusters } from './data/dashboard-mock-data';`
`test.beforeEach(async ({ page }) => {`
`  await page.route('**/api/nodes', route => route.fulfill({ json: mockNodes }));`
`  await page.route('**/api/clusters', route => route.fulfill({ json: mockClusters }));`
`  await page.goto('/pi-controller');`
`});`
tasks.testStrategy: Verify that the `dashboard.spec.ts` and `navigation.spec.ts` files are created in the `tests/` directory. Run a simple placeholder test within one of the files that navigates to the dashboard and confirms the page title. Ensure the `page.route` intercepts are being called successfully by adding a `console.log` inside the handler during the test run.

tasks.title: Test Dashboard Overview Metrics Display
tasks.description: Implement tests in `dashboard.spec.ts` to verify that all overview metric cards (Total Nodes, Total Clusters, Average CPU/Temp) and the Top 5 Nodes list are rendered correctly on the dashboard.
tasks.details: Using Playwright, navigate to the dashboard page. Use `data-testid` attributes for stable selectors as shown in the PRD. For each metric card, use `page.locator('[data-testid="..."]')` to find the element and `expect(locator).toBeVisible()` to assert its presence. The test should confirm the static elements and labels are displayed, but will not yet validate the accuracy of the data.
tasks.testStrategy: Run the Playwright test and confirm that it passes. The test should check for the visibility of locators like `[data-testid="total-nodes"]`, `[data-testid="total-clusters"]`, `[data-testid="avg-cpu"]`, `[data-testid="avg-temp"]`, and `[data-testid="top-nodes-list"]`. Manually inspect the test report screenshot to confirm the UI components are rendered as expected.

tasks.title: Test Dashboard Overview Metrics Accuracy
tasks.description: Implement tests in `dashboard.spec.ts` to validate that the data displayed in the overview metric cards is calculated and formatted correctly based on the provided mock data.
tasks.details:
Extend the previous tests to read the content of the metric cards using `locator.textContent()`. Compare these values against the expected values derived from the `mockNodes` and `mockClusters` data. For averages, create simple utility functions (e.g., `calculateAvgCpu(nodes)`) to compute the expected result. Use `expect(value).toBe()` for counts and `expect(value).toBeCloseTo()` for floating-point numbers like averages.

Example check:
`const totalNodes = await page.locator('[data-testid="total-nodes"]').textContent();`
`expect(parseInt(totalNodes!)).toBe(mockNodes.length);`
tasks.testStrategy: The test will pass if the text content of each metric card on the dashboard exactly matches the values calculated from the source mock data. Check integer counts, floating-point averages (with a specified precision), and the names of the nodes in the 'Top 5 Nodes' list.

tasks.title: Test Sidebar Navigation State and Interaction
tasks.description: Create tests in `navigation.spec.ts` to verify the sidebar's core interactions, such as expanding and collapsing, and ensuring the active route is correctly highlighted.
tasks.details: Use locators to target the sidebar container and the expand/collapse button. Simulate a click and assert that a class or attribute on the sidebar container changes (e.g., `aria-expanded`). For active route highlighting, navigate to a specific page and then check that the corresponding `<a>` tag in the sidebar has the 'active' class or `aria-current='page'` attribute.
tasks.testStrategy: Run tests that (1) click the collapse button and verify the sidebar's width or class changes, (2) click the expand button and verify it returns to the original state, and (3) navigate to '/pi-controller/nodes' and assert that only the 'Nodes' link in the sidebar has the active state indicator.

tasks.title: Test Sidebar Menu Navigation Routing
tasks.description: Implement a comprehensive test in `navigation.spec.ts` that iterates through all sidebar menu items and verifies that clicking each one navigates the user to the correct URL.
tasks.details: Create an array of test cases, where each object contains the link label and the expected route (e.g., `{ label: 'Clusters', route: '/pi-controller/clusters' }`). Loop through this array. In each iteration, use `page.getByRole('link', { name: item.label }).click()` and then assert the URL with `await expect(page).toHaveURL(new RegExp(item.route));`. This ensures all primary navigation paths are functional.
tasks.testStrategy: The test passes if, for every menu item in the sidebar, the application navigates to the expected URL and the page loads without errors. The Playwright trace should show a sequence of navigations corresponding to the menu items.

tasks.title: Test Node Detail View Selector and Initial Load
tasks.description: In `dashboard.spec.ts`, create a test to verify the node selector dropdown on the node detail page. It should list all mock nodes and load the correct node's data upon selection.
tasks.details: First, navigate to a specific node's URL, e.g., `/pi-controller/nodes/node-1`. Verify the page title or a header contains the node's name. Then, click the node selector dropdown. Assert that the number of options in the dropdown matches the length of `mockNodes`. Select a different node from the dropdown and verify the URL updates and the header changes to the newly selected node's name.
tasks.testStrategy: The test should successfully (1) load a node page directly via URL, (2) open the node selector dropdown, (3) verify all mock nodes are present as options, (4) select a new node, and (5) confirm the page content updates to reflect the new selection by checking a unique identifier like the node's name in a H1 tag.

tasks.title: Test Node Detail View Tab Switching
tasks.description: Implement tests in `dashboard.spec.ts` to ensure that switching between the 'Overview', 'GPIO Control', and 'Monitoring' tabs on the node detail page works correctly.
tasks.details: On a node detail page, locate the tab buttons. The 'Overview' tab should be active by default; assert this by checking for an `aria-selected="true"` attribute. Then, programmatically click the 'GPIO Control' tab. Assert it becomes the selected tab and a unique element within its panel (e.g., `[data-testid="gpio-pins"]`) becomes visible. Repeat this process for the 'Monitoring' tab, checking for `[data-testid="monitoring-panel"]`.
tasks.testStrategy: The test passes if clicking each tab button correctly updates its `aria-selected` state and makes the content panel for that tab visible, while hiding the content of the other tabs. Use `locator.click()` and `expect(locator).toBeVisible()` assertions.

tasks.title: Test Node Detail View Metrics Display
tasks.description: Verify that the metrics, status badges, and progress bars within the node detail 'Overview' tab display accurate information for the selected node.
tasks.details: After navigating to a node's detail page, use locators to read the values for status, role, and various metrics (CPU, temperature, etc.). Compare these values against the corresponding node object in the `mockNodes` array. For progress bars, check the `aria-valuenow` attribute to verify the displayed percentage matches the mock data.
tasks.testStrategy: The test is successful if all static badges (e.g., 'Status: Online', 'Role: Master') and dynamic metric values on the page match the data from the mock object for the currently selected node. Assert that progress bar `aria-valuenow` attributes are correct.

tasks.title: Test Dashboard Quick Action Buttons
tasks.description: Implement tests for the quick action buttons on the main dashboard to ensure they navigate to the correct pages or trigger the expected UI changes.
tasks.details: Locate the quick action buttons (e.g., 'Add New Node', 'Manage Clusters') on the main dashboard. For each button, simulate a click. If the button is a navigation link, assert that the URL changes to the expected path using `expect(page).toHaveURL()`. If it's supposed to open a modal, assert that the modal container becomes visible.
tasks.testStrategy: Run the test and verify that clicking each quick action button results in the correct navigation event or modal display. Check the URL after each click for navigation buttons. For modals, check for the presence of a modal-specific locator.

tasks.title: Test Real-Time Metric Updates
tasks.description: Implement a test to simulate and verify real-time metric updates on the dashboard. The test will mock an updated API response and assert that the UI reflects the new data without a full page reload.
tasks.details:
Use `page.route()` to handle the initial data request. After the page loads, re-configure the route to provide updated mock data (e.g., a node's CPU usage changes from 50% to 90%). To trigger the data fetch, you may need to wait for a polling interval or simulate an event. Finally, assert that the corresponding metric display on the page has been updated to the new value (90%).

Pseudo-code:
`// Initial setup`
`await page.route('**/api/nodes', route => route.fulfill({ json: initialMockNodes }));`
`await page.goto('/pi-controller');`
`await expect(page.locator('#cpu-usage')).toHaveText('50%');`

`// Setup updated mock and trigger update`
`await page.route('**/api/nodes', route => route.fulfill({ json: updatedMockNodes }));`
`// Wait for polling, e.g., await page.waitForTimeout(5100);` 

`// Assert update`
`await expect(page.locator('#cpu-usage')).toHaveText('90%');`
tasks.testStrategy: The test passes if the UI metric value updates dynamically after the mocked API starts returning new data. The test must confirm the initial value, mock the new response, wait for the update to occur, and then confirm the displayed value has changed to the new mock value.

tasks.title: Create Mock Cluster Data for Testing

tasks.testStrategy: Run the test and confirm it passes. The test should successfully navigate to the cluster page, mock the API response, and verify that the number of rendered cluster cards matches the number of objects in the mock data file.

tasks.title: Implement Cluster Filtering by Type Test
tasks.description: Write a test within `clusters.spec.ts` to validate the functionality of the filter tabs (All, Kubernetes, Docker, Custom). This covers PRD subtask 4.
tasks.details: In `clusters.spec.ts`, create a new `test` block. Following the PRD example, the test should click on each filter tab (e.g., `page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Kubernetes' }).click();`). After clicking, iterate through the visible `.cluster-card` elements and assert that the text content of the element with `data-testid="cluster-type"` matches the selected filter. Repeat for 'Docker' and 'Custom' tabs. Use the mock data from task 112 which contains a mix of cluster types.
tasks.testStrategy: Execute the test suite. The test should pass for each filter type, confirming that clicking a filter tab updates the UI to show only clusters of that specific type.

tasks.title: Implement Cluster Search Functionality Test
tasks.description: Add a test to `clusters.spec.ts` to verify that users can search for clusters by name and that the list updates correctly to show only matching results. This covers PRD subtask 3.
tasks.details: In `clusters.spec.ts`, create a test that locates the search input field, likely via a role or placeholder selector like `page.getByPlaceholder('Search clusters...')`. Use `locator.fill('Kube-Prod')` with a search term that matches one of the mock clusters. Assert that only the expected cluster(s) are visible. Use an assertion like `expect(page.locator('.cluster-card')).toHaveCount(1);` and `expect(page.locator('.cluster-card')).toContainText('Kube-Prod-West');`. Also test a non-matching search term and assert that zero results are shown.

tasks.title: Test Cluster Card Content and 'New Cluster' Button Navigation
tasks.description: Verify that individual cluster cards display the correct information and that the 'New Cluster' button navigates to the cluster creation wizard. This covers PRD subtasks 5 and 6.
tasks.details: In `clusters.spec.ts`, add a test to inspect the first cluster card rendered from the mock data. tasks.testStrategy: The card content test should pass, confirming data binding is correct. The button navigation test should pass, confirming the user is correctly routed to the start of the creation wizard.

tasks.title: Setup Cluster Creation Test and Wizard Navigation Logic
tasks.description: Create the `cluster-creation.spec.ts` file and implement tests to verify basic navigation (Next, Back) through the multi-step wizard without submitting data. This covers PRD subtasks 7 and 8.
tasks.details: Create `tests/e2e/cluster-creation.spec.ts`. To promote maintainability, create a simple Page Object Model (POM) for the wizard. tasks.testStrategy: Run the new spec file. The tests should successfully navigate forward and backward through the wizard steps, confirming the core navigation logic works before testing form interactions.

tasks.title: Implement Wizard Form Input Validation Tests
tasks.description: Test the form validation at each step of the creation wizard, such as required fields and format validation. This covers PRD subtask 9.
tasks.details: In `cluster-creation.spec.ts`, add tests for form validation. For Step 1, click the 'Next' button without filling in the cluster name. tasks.title: Implement End-to-End Successful Cluster Creation Test
tasks.description: Create a 'happy path' test that completes all steps of the wizard with valid data and verifies the successful creation of a new cluster. This covers PRD subtasks 10, 11, and 12.
tasks.details: In `cluster-creation.spec.ts`, write a test that follows the PRD example script. It should mock any necessary API calls for node selection (`page.route('/api/nodes', ...)`). The test will fill out each form step with valid data, navigate through to the final review step, and click the 'Create' button. Mock the final POST request to the cluster creation endpoint to return a success response. Assert that a success notification is visible and that the page redirects back to the main cluster list.
tasks.testStrategy: The test should run from start to finish without errors, successfully simulating the creation of a cluster and verifying the correct post-creation UI state (toast message and redirection).

tasks.title: Implement Cluster Details Page Verification Test
tasks.description: Write a test to ensure that clicking on a cluster from the list navigates to its details page and displays the correct information. This covers PRD subtask 13.
tasks.details: In `clusters.spec.ts`, add a test that uses the mocked cluster list. The test will click on the first cluster card (`page.locator('.cluster-card').first().click();`). It should then mock the API call for a single cluster, e.g., `page.route('/api/clusters/c1', ...)`, using the corresponding object from `clusters.ts`. On the details page, assert that the displayed name, type, and other properties match the mocked data. Use `expect(page.locator('h1')).toContainText('Kube-Prod-West');`.
tasks.testStrategy: Run the test. It must successfully navigate to the details page and verify that all key pieces of information for the selected cluster are rendered accurately.

tasks.title: Implement Cluster Edit and Delete Operations Test
tasks.description: Add tests to `cluster-creation.spec.ts` or a new `cluster-management.spec.ts` to cover the edit and delete functionalities for a cluster. This covers PRD subtask 14.
tasks.details: For the delete test: navigate to a cluster details page, click the 'Delete' button, and confirm any modal dialog. Mock the `DELETE /api/clusters/:id` request to return a 200 OK. Assert that the user is redirected to the cluster list and the cluster is no longer present. For the edit test: navigate to the details page, click 'Edit', change a field (e.g., the description), and save. Mock the `PUT /api/clusters/:id` request. Assert that a success message is shown and the updated information is displayed.
tasks.testStrategy: The delete test should verify the cluster is removed from the UI after deletion. The edit test should verify that submitted changes are reflected on the details page after saving.

tasks.title: Create Comprehensive Mock Node Data for E2E Tests
tasks.description: Develop a set of mock node data to be used across all node management tests. This data should cover all possible node states (Online, Offline, Warning), roles, and include realistic metrics for both managed and discovered nodes.
tasks.details: Create a file at `e2e/mocks/nodes.ts`. This file will export arrays of node objects. For example, `mockNodes` for the main list and `mockDiscoveredNodes` for the discovery panel. tasks.testStrategy: Review the mock data file to ensure it covers all required test permutations (different statuses, roles, edge cases). A simple unit test can be added to validate the data structure if it becomes programmatically generated. The primary validation will be its successful use in subsequent E2E tests.

tasks.title: Implement E2E Test for Node List Display and Statistics Cards
tasks.description: Create the `nodes.spec.ts` test file and implement a test to verify that the main node list page correctly displays nodes from a mock API and that the summary statistics cards (Total, Online, Warning, Offline) show the correct counts.
tasks.details: In a new file `e2e/nodes.spec.ts`, use the `authenticatedPage` fixture. Before navigating to `/pi-controller/nodes`, set up `await page.route('**/api/nodes', route => route.fulfill({ json: mockNodes }));` using the mock data from task 122. Verify the number of `.node-card` elements rendered matches the length of `mockNodes`. Calculate expected counts from the mock data and assert that the text content of the statistics cards (e.g., `[data-testid="stat-online"]`) matches.
tasks.testStrategy: Assert that the number of rendered node cards equals the number of nodes in the mock data. For each statistic card, assert that the displayed number correctly reflects the count of nodes with the corresponding status in the mock data.

tasks.title: Implement E2E Test for Node Search Functionality
tasks.description: Test the search functionality on the nodes page. The test should verify that typing a hostname or IP address into the search bar correctly filters the list of displayed nodes in real-time.
tasks.details: Within `nodes.spec.ts`, create a new `test` block. Use the same `page.route()` setup with mock data. Select a specific node from the mock data. Then, clear the input and assert the full list is visible again. Repeat for an IP address.
tasks.testStrategy: The test passes if: 1. Typing a known hostname filters the list to the single matching node. 2. Typing a known IP address does the same. 3. Clearing the search input restores the full list. 4. Typing a non-matching query shows an empty state.

tasks.title: Implement E2E Test for Node Filtering by Status and Role
tasks.description: Test the status and role filter dropdowns. The test should verify that selecting a status (e.g., 'online') or a role correctly filters the list of displayed nodes.
tasks.details: In `nodes.spec.ts`, add a test following the PRD's example. Use mock data from task 122 containing a mix of statuses and roles. Reset the filter and repeat for other statuses and for the role filter.
tasks.testStrategy: For each selectable filter option (e.g., status: 'online', role: 'master'), assert that all visible nodes in the list strictly match that criterion. Verify that selecting the default 'All' option displays all nodes from the mock data.

tasks.title: Implement E2E Test for Node Card Metrics Display
tasks.description: Verify that each individual node card correctly displays the key metrics (e.g., CPU, memory, disk usage) provided in the mock data.
tasks.details: In `nodes.spec.ts`, add a test that focuses on the content of a single `.node-card`. Locate a specific card, for example, `page.locator('.node-card', { hasText: 'pi-node-1' })`. Within that card's scope, locate the elements for metrics like `[data-testid="cpu-usage"]`. Assert that their text content or value correctly formats and matches the corresponding values in the mock data object for 'pi-node-1'.
tasks.testStrategy: The test passes if the metrics (CPU, Memory, Disk) displayed on the UI for a representative node card exactly match the values defined in the mock data for that node.

tasks.title: Create Node Adoption Test Suite and Test Discovery Panel
tasks.description: Create the `node-adoption.spec.ts` test file. Implement the first test to verify the node discovery panel can be opened and correctly displays a list of discovered, unadopted nodes from a mock API.
tasks.details: Create a new file `e2e/node-adoption.spec.ts`. Use the `authenticatedPage` fixture. tasks.title: Implement E2E Test for Discovered Node Adoption Workflow
tasks.description: Implement the end-to-end test for adopting a node from the discovery panel, which includes filling in credentials in a modal and confirming the adoption.
