tasks.title: Implement E2E Test for Manual Node Entry and Adoption
tasks.description: Test the workflow for manually adding a node via its own dialog. This involves opening the dialog, filling in the node's details and credentials, and submitting the form.
tasks.details: In `node-adoption.spec.ts`, create a test to handle the manual flow. The test will click a button like 'Add Node Manually' to open a dialog. Mock the adoption API endpoint (`POST /api/nodes`) to return a success response. Fill in the form fields (e.g., IP address, username, password). Click the confirm button and assert that the API call was made with the correct payload from the form. Finally, verify a success notification is displayed.
tasks.testStrategy: The test passes if the manual adoption form can be filled and submitted, a `POST` request is sent to the adoption endpoint with the form data, and a success notification is shown to the user upon a successful mock response.

tasks.title: Implement E2E Test for Node Action Buttons
tasks.description: Test the action buttons available on each node card, such as 'Monitor' and 'Hardware', to ensure they trigger the correct operations or navigations.
tasks.details: In `nodes.spec.ts`, add a test for actions on a managed node from the mock data. For the 'Monitor' button, click it and assert that the page navigates to the correct URL (e.g., `/pi-controller/nodes/uuid-1/monitoring`) using `await expect(page).toHaveURL(...)`. Do the same for the 'Hardware' button. Mock any necessary API calls for the destination pages to prevent test failures from unrelated issues.
tasks.testStrategy: For each action button that causes navigation, assert that the browser's URL changes to the expected path. For buttons that open modals or trigger other UI changes, assert that the expected element becomes visible.

tasks.title: Implement E2E Test for Real-time Node Metrics Updates
tasks.description: Verify that the metrics (CPU, RAM, etc.) on the node cards update automatically based on a refresh interval without requiring a full page reload.
tasks.details: In `nodes.spec.ts`, create a test that mocks the `/api/nodes` endpoint twice. The first `page.route` call will be a one-time handler (`route.fulfill({ json: initialNodes })`). The second will be a persistent handler (`page.route('**/api/nodes', route => route.fulfill({ json: updatedNodes }))`) that provides updated metrics. After the initial load, use `page.clock.fastForward('30s')` or a similar Playwright time-traveling utility to simulate the passage of time. Then, assert that the metric values on a specific node card have changed to reflect the `updatedNodes` data.
tasks.testStrategy: The test will pass if, after advancing the clock to trigger a data refresh, the metric values displayed in the UI update to match a second set of mock data, confirming the real-time update mechanism works as expected.

tasks.title: Setup Test Files and Comprehensive GPIO Mocking
tasks.description: Create the necessary Playwright test files (`hardware.spec.ts`, `gpio-control.spec.ts`) and implement a robust mocking strategy for the hardware API endpoints. This includes creating mock data for different nodes, pin configurations (input/output, high/low, read-only), and system states.
tasks.details: Use Playwright's `page.route()` to intercept API calls like `/api/v1/nodes/:nodeId/gpio` and `/api/v1/nodes/:nodeId/system-info`. Create a separate mock data file (e.g., `tests/mocks/hardware.ts`) that exports different scenarios for GPIO pins (including LEDs, Buttons, Sensors, Relays as mentioned in the PRD) and system metrics. The mock handler should be able to return successful responses, error responses (e.g., 500), and different pin states to facilitate comprehensive testing. Ensure mock data covers read-only pins (mode: 'input').
tasks.testStrategy: Run a simple test that navigates to a hardware page and asserts that a mocked API call was intercepted. Verify that the test runner can access and use the mock data structures. No UI assertions are needed for this task, focus solely on the mocking infrastructure.

tasks.title: Test Hardware Page Layout and Node Selection
tasks.description: Verify the basic structure of the hardware control page, including the presence of a node selection dropdown, system overview cards, and navigation tabs for GPIO, System Info, and Network.
tasks.details: In `hardware.spec.ts`, write a test that navigates to `/pi-controller/hardware`. Use a mock for the list of available nodes. Test that the dropdown is visible and populated. Select a different node and verify the URL updates correctly (e.g., to `/pi-controller/hardware/node-2`). Assert that the main content area loads and that the system overview cards (CPU Temp, Memory, etc.) and the three navigation tabs are visible.
tasks.testStrategy: Assert visibility of key elements using `expect(locator).toBeVisible()`. Check that the node selection dropdown contains the expected items from the mock data. Verify URL changes upon selection using `expect(page).toHaveURL()`. Ensure the main tabs for 'GPIO Pins', 'System Info', and 'Network' are present.

tasks.title: Implement GPIO Pin List Display Test
tasks.description: Test that the GPIO Pins tab correctly renders the list of pins based on the mocked API response. This includes verifying the pin number, name, status badge (HIGH/LOW), and category badge (LED, Button, etc.).
tasks.details: In `gpio-control.spec.ts`, set up a test that routes the GPIO API call to return a specific set of mock pin data. Navigate to the hardware page and click the 'GPIO Pins' tab. Iterate through the mock data and verify that a corresponding UI element exists for each pin. Use `data-` attributes like `data-pin='17'` for stable locators. Check that the text content of the status (`data-testid='pin-status'`) and category badges are correct.
tasks.testStrategy: Use `locator.all()` to get all pin elements and assert the count matches the mock data. For a few specific pins from the mock data, assert that their name, status text ('HIGH'/'LOW'), and category text ('LED'/'Sensor') are rendered correctly.

tasks.title: Implement GPIO Pin Toggle Functionality Test
tasks.description: Verify that a user can toggle the state of an output pin from LOW to HIGH and vice-versa, and that the UI updates accordingly after a successful API response.
tasks.details: Using the test setup from the previous task, locate a toggleable pin (e.g., `data-mode='output'`). Get its initial state via `aria-checked`. Click the toggle button. Set up the mock response for the POST/PUT request to `/api/v1/gpio` to return a success status and the new pin state. Use `page.waitForResponse()` to ensure the API call has completed. Assert that the `aria-checked` attribute has changed. Also, verify the status badge text updates to reflect the new state ('HIGH' or 'LOW').
tasks.testStrategy: 1. Get initial 'aria-checked' value. 2. Click toggle. 3. `await page.waitForResponse(...)`. 4. Get new 'aria-checked' value and assert it's different from the initial value. 5. Assert that the `data-testid='pin-status'` badge text has been updated.

tasks.title: Implement Pin State Persistence Test
tasks.description: Ensure that the state of a GPIO pin persists after a page reload, correctly reflecting the state from the (mocked) backend.
tasks.details: This test will simulate a state change and then verify it's correctly loaded on a subsequent visit. First, perform a toggle action as in the previous task. Then, `await page.reload()`. The mock for the initial GET request to `/api/v1/nodes/:nodeId/gpio` should now be configured to return the *new* state. After the reload, locate the same pin and assert that its toggle and badge reflect the new, persisted state without any user interaction.
tasks.testStrategy: 1. Mock initial state (e.g., pin 17 is LOW). 2. Mock the toggle API call to succeed. 3. Mock the subsequent GET request to return the new state (pin 17 is HIGH). 4. Click toggle. 5. Reload page. 6. Assert pin 17 toggle is now in the HIGH state.

tasks.title: Implement Read-Only Pin Protection Test
tasks.description: Verify that pins configured as read-only (e.g., input mode) cannot be toggled. The toggle control should be disabled, and a tooltip should explain why.
tasks.details: Use mock data where at least one pin has `"mode": "input"`. Locate this pin in the UI, possibly using a selector like `.gpio-pin[data-mode='input'] button`. Use Playwright's `expect(locator).toBeDisabled()` assertion to verify the button is not clickable. Then, trigger the tooltip by using `locator.hover()` and assert that a tooltip element becomes visible (`[role='tooltip']`) and contains explanatory text like 'read-only' or 'input pin'.
tasks.testStrategy: 1. Locate a pin designated as read-only in the mock data. 2. Assert its toggle button is disabled. 3. Hover over the button. 4. Assert a tooltip appears. 5. Assert the tooltip's text content matches the expected explanation.

tasks.title: Implement GPIO Operation Error Handling Test
tasks.description: Test the UI's behavior when an API call to toggle a GPIO pin fails. The UI should display an error message and the pin's state should revert to its original position.
tasks.details: Locate a toggleable pin. Get its initial state. Configure `page.route()` for the toggle endpoint (`/api/v1/gpio`) to return a 500 server error response. Click the toggle button. `await page.waitForResponse()` for the failed response. Assert that an error notification (e.g., a toast or alert) appears with a relevant message. Crucially, assert that the pin's toggle `aria-checked` attribute and status badge have *not* changed from their initial state.
tasks.testStrategy: 1. Get initial pin state. 2. Mock API to return a 500 error. 3. Click toggle. 4. Assert an error message is visible. 5. Re-check the pin's state and assert it has not changed.

tasks.title: Implement System Information Tab Accuracy Test
tasks.description: Validate that the 'System Info' tab and the overview cards accurately display the data provided by the mocked system information endpoint.
tasks.details: In `hardware.spec.ts`, create a test that mocks the `/api/v1/nodes/:nodeId/system-info` endpoint with specific values (e.g., CPU Temp: '45.2°C', Memory: '35%', Load: '0.75', Uptime: '12 days'). Navigate to the page and check the overview cards. Then, click the 'System Info' tab and verify that the detailed information presented matches the full mocked data object. Use `data-testid` selectors for stability.
tasks.testStrategy: For each metric (CPU Temp, Memory, Load, Uptime), locate the corresponding element on the page and use `expect(locator).toContainText()` to assert that it displays the value from the mock data.

tasks.title: Implement Network Tab Information Test
tasks.description: Verify that the 'Network' tab correctly displays network configuration details, such as IP address, MAC address, and connection status, based on mocked API data.
tasks.details: Similar to the system info test, mock an endpoint for network data (e.g., `/api/v1/nodes/:nodeId/network-info`). The mock data should include fields like `ipAddress`, `macAddress`, `hostname`, `ssid`, etc. Write a test that navigates to the hardware page, clicks the 'Network' tab, and asserts that the displayed values match the mocked data.
tasks.testStrategy: Locate the elements displaying network information on the 'Network' tab. For each piece of data (IP, MAC, etc.), assert that the element's text content matches the corresponding value in the mock object.

tasks.title: Refactor Tests using Page Object Model (POM)
tasks.description: Refactor the newly created tests into a Page Object Model (POM) pattern to improve maintainability and readability. Create classes for the Hardware Page and its components.
tasks.details: Create a new file, e.g., `tests/pages/HardwarePage.ts`. In this file, define a class `HardwarePage` that encapsulates locators and actions. For example: `this.gpioPinsTab = page.locator('button:has-text("GPIO Pins")')` and `async togglePin(pinNumber) { ... }`. Update the `hardware.spec.ts` and `gpio-control.spec.ts` files to import and use this page object, simplifying the test logic and removing direct `page.locator` calls from the test bodies.
tasks.testStrategy: After refactoring, run the entire test suite. All tests must pass without any changes to their core logic. The success of this task is measured by the improved structure of the code and the continued passing of all previously written tests.

tasks.title: Setup Settings Test Files and Mock Data
tasks.description: Create the necessary Playwright test files (`settings.spec.ts`, `config-import-export.spec.ts`) and define mock configuration data for consistent testing.
tasks.details: In the `tests/` directory (or equivalent e2e test folder), create two new files: `settings.spec.ts` for UI and form tests, and `config-import-export.spec.ts` for file operations. Create a new file, `tests/mocks/settings.data.ts`, to export mock configuration objects. This should include a 'default' config, a 'validUpdate' config, and potentially invalid data snippets for validation tests. Use Playwright's `test.describe` to group related tests within each file. Ensure the standard test setup, including the `authenticatedPage` fixture, is imported and used.
tasks.testStrategy: Verify that both spec files are created in the project's test directory. Run the test runner (e.g., `npx playwright test`) and confirm that it discovers the new test files, even if they contain no tests yet. Check that the mock data file exports the expected configuration objects correctly.

tasks.title: Implement Basic UI and Tab Navigation Tests
tasks.description: Write tests to verify that the settings page loads correctly, displays all configuration sections, and that users can switch between the 'Form Editor' and 'YAML Editor' tabs.
tasks.details: In `settings.spec.ts`, add a test case using `test('should display settings page elements', ...)` that navigates to `/pi-controller/settings`. Use `expect(page.locator(...)).toBeVisible()` to assert that the main heading, Form/YAML tabs, and key configuration sections (e.g., General, Network) are present. Create another test `test('should switch between Form and YAML tabs', ...)` that clicks on the 'YAML Editor' tab and verifies its content area becomes visible, then clicks back to the 'Form Editor' tab and confirms its visibility.
tasks.testStrategy: Run the tests and ensure they pass. The first test should confirm the presence of key static elements on the page. The second test should programmatically click each tab and assert that the active tab state changes and the corresponding content panel (e.g., a form for the form editor, a text area/code editor for the YAML editor) is visible.

tasks.title: Test General Settings Form Update and Persistence
tasks.description: Implement a test to update settings via the form, save the changes, and verify that the new configuration persists after a page reload.
tasks.details: In `settings.spec.ts`, implement the 'should update general settings' test scenario from the PRD. Use the mock data from `settings.data.ts` to populate the form fields. Use `page.fill('input[name="hostname"]', ...)` and `page.selectOption('select[name="timezone"]', ...)` to update the form. Click the 'Save Changes' button and use `expect(page.locator('.success-toast')).toBeVisible()` to wait for and verify the success notification. Then, call `page.reload()` and assert that the input fields retain their new values using `expect(page.locator(...)).toHaveValue(...)`.
tasks.testStrategy: The test should successfully fill the form, save, and confirm the success message. After reloading, the assertions must confirm that the values entered during the test are still present in the form fields, proving persistence.

tasks.title: Implement Form Input Validation Tests
tasks.description: Test the form's input validation rules by submitting empty required fields and incorrectly formatted data, ensuring appropriate error messages are displayed.
tasks.details: In `settings.spec.ts`, create a `test.describe('Form Validation', ...)` block. Add test cases for each validation rule. For required fields, clear the input using `page.locator(...).clear()` and click 'Save Changes', then assert that a specific error message locator becomes visible next to the field. For format validation (e.g., invalid hostname characters), use `page.fill(...)` with invalid data and verify the corresponding error message appears. The 'Save Changes' button should ideally be disabled until the form is valid, which should also be tested.
tasks.testStrategy: For each validation scenario, the test must confirm two things: 1) An explicit and user-friendly error message is displayed for the invalid field. 2) The form submission is prevented (e.g., no success toast appears, and no navigation occurs).

tasks.title: Implement YAML Configuration Export Test
tasks.description: Verify that clicking the 'Export YAML' button downloads a correctly formatted YAML file containing the current configuration.
tasks.details: In `config-import-export.spec.ts`, implement the 'should export configuration as YAML' test from the PRD. Use Playwright's `page.waitForEvent('download')` to capture the download event triggered by clicking the 'Export YAML' button. Assert that the downloaded file has a `.yaml` or `.yml` extension. Use the `download.path()` method to get the temporary file path and Node's `fs.promises.readFile` to read its content. Use a library like `js-yaml` to parse the content and verify that key-value pairs (e.g., 'hostname', 'timezone') match the current settings in the UI.
tasks.testStrategy: The test passes if a file download is successfully initiated, the file name is correct, and its contents are valid YAML that accurately reflects the configuration shown on the settings page before the export was triggered.

tasks.title: Implement Valid YAML Configuration Import Test
tasks.description: Test the functionality of importing a valid YAML file. The form fields should update to reflect the values from the imported file.
tasks.details: In `config-import-export.spec.ts`, create a test 'should import a valid YAML configuration'. First, create a valid `config.yaml` file on the fly using `fs.promises.writeFile` and data from your mocks. Then, use `page.locator('input[type="file"]').setInputFiles('path/to/your/config.yaml')`. This may require making the file input element visible first if it's hidden. After the file is selected, the UI should update automatically or after a confirmation step. Assert that the values in the form inputs now match the data from the imported YAML file.
tasks.testStrategy: The test should successfully upload the mock YAML file. After the import action, assertions checking the values of the form fields (e.g., `expect(page.locator('input[name="hostname"]')).toHaveValue(...)`) must pass, confirming the UI state was updated from the file.

tasks.title: Implement Invalid YAML Import Validation Test
tasks.description: Verify that the application handles the import of malformed or invalid YAML files gracefully by displaying a clear error message.
tasks.details: In `config-import-export.spec.ts`, create a test for invalid imports. Create a temporary file with malformed YAML content (e.g., incorrect indentation, invalid syntax). Use `setInputFiles` to upload this invalid file. The application should detect the invalid format and display an error message (e.g., a toast notification or an inline error). Assert that this specific error message locator is visible. Also, assert that the form fields have not changed from their original values.
tasks.testStrategy: The test passes if, after attempting to import a broken YAML file, a specific error notification is shown to the user, and the existing configuration in the form remains unchanged.

tasks.title: Test Synchronization Between Form and YAML Editors
tasks.description: Ensure that changes made in the form editor are reflected in the YAML editor, and vice-versa, when switching between tabs.
tasks.details: In `settings.spec.ts`, create a new test 'should sync changes between editors'. First, change a value in the form editor (e.g., update the hostname). Do not save. Switch to the 'YAML Editor' tab. Retrieve the content of the YAML editor (this might require `page.locator(...).inputValue()` or `page.evaluate(...)` depending on the editor component) and assert that it contains the updated hostname. Then, reverse the process: modify a value in the YAML editor, switch to the 'Form Editor' tab, and assert that the corresponding form input has been updated.
tasks.testStrategy: The test requires checking the state of one editor after a change is made in the other. It passes if the values are correctly propagated in both directions (Form -> YAML and YAML -> Form) upon switching tabs.

tasks.title: Implement 'Reset to Defaults' Functionality Test
tasks.description: Verify that the 'Reset to Defaults' button reverts all settings in both the form and YAML editors to their default values.
tasks.details: In `settings.spec.ts`, create a test for the reset functionality. First, modify a few settings in the form to deviate from the default state. Click the 'Reset to Defaults' button (and confirm any dialog if present). Assert that the form inputs have reverted to the default values defined in your mock data. Switch to the 'YAML Editor' tab and verify its content also reflects the default configuration.
tasks.testStrategy: The test is successful if, after making changes and clicking 'Reset', all tested form fields and the YAML editor content match a known, predefined default state.

tasks.title: Refactor Tests with Page Object Model (POM)
tasks.description: Refactor the implemented tests to use the Page Object Model (POM) pattern for better maintainability and readability by encapsulating page selectors and actions.
tasks.details: Create a new file, `tests/pages/settings.page.ts`. Define a `SettingsPage` class. Move all selectors (e.g., `hostnameInput = page.locator('input[name="hostname"]')`) into this class. Create methods for common actions (e.g., `async updateHostname(hostname: string)`, `async saveChanges()`, `async exportYaml()`). Refactor the spec files to import and instantiate this `SettingsPage` class, and replace direct `page.locator` calls with calls to the methods on the page object, e.g., `await settingsPage.updateHostname('new-name')`.
tasks.testStrategy: After refactoring, run the entire test suite for settings. All existing tests must continue to pass. The success of this task is measured by the improved code structure and the continued correctness of the tests, not by new test coverage.

tasks.title: Create Documentation Test Suite File
tasks.description: Create a new Playwright test file named `documentation.spec.ts` to house all tests related to the documentation and help pages.
tasks.details: In the `tests/` directory (or equivalent e2e test directory confirmed by codebase analysis), create a new file `documentation.spec.ts`. Add the basic Playwright test structure, importing `test` and `expect` from `@playwright/test`. Define a `test.describe` block for 'Documentation and Help Pages' to group related tests.
tasks.testStrategy: Run `npx playwright test tests/documentation.spec.ts` and confirm the test runner discovers the new file and runs the empty suite without errors.

tasks.title: Implement Documentation Page Load Test
tasks.description: Add a test to verify that the main documentation page loads successfully for an authenticated user without any console errors.
tasks.details: Using the existing `authenticatedPage` fixture, write a test that navigates to `/pi-controller/documentation`. The test should assert that the page's main title (e.g., `h1`) is visible and contains the text 'Documentation'. This confirms basic routing and page rendering. This is a foundational smoke test.
tasks.testStrategy: The test should pass when the documentation page is reachable and renders correctly. The test should fail if the page returns a 4xx/5xx error or if the main heading is not found.

tasks.title: Implement Test for All Documentation Sections
tasks.description: Create a test to ensure all primary sections of the documentation are present and visible on the page.
tasks.details: Based on the PRD, create an array of expected section titles: `['Overview', 'Getting Started', 'API Reference', 'Troubleshooting']`. Use a loop to iterate through this array. For each title, use `expect(page.locator('h2', { hasText: section })).toBeVisible()` to assert that a corresponding `h2` element exists and is visible. This approach is scalable if more sections are added.
tasks.testStrategy: The test should pass if all specified `h2` elements are found. Introduce a typo into one of the expected section titles in the test code to ensure it fails as expected. Remove a section from the page's source to verify test failure.

tasks.title: Implement Link Navigation Test
tasks.description: Verify that all navigation links within the documentation side menu or table of contents navigate to the correct page section or URL.
tasks.details: First, locate the container for the navigation links (e.g., `nav[aria-label='Documentation']`). Get all `<a>` tags within it using `page.locator('nav >> a').all()`. Loop through the links. For each link, get its `href` attribute. Click the link using `link.click()`. Then, assert that the page URL has been updated correctly using `expect(page).toHaveURL(/.*#expected-anchor/)` for anchor links or the full path for page links.
tasks.testStrategy: Run the test and ensure it clicks through all navigation items and verifies the URL changes accordingly. Manually break a link on the page and confirm the test fails with a URL mismatch or timeout.

tasks.title: Implement Code Example Formatting Test
tasks.description: Test that code examples are rendered correctly and have the proper formatting, likely applied by a syntax highlighting library.
tasks.details: Locate code blocks on the page, which are typically within `<pre><code>` elements. A good selector might be `pre > code`. Assert that at least one such element exists. Then, check for the presence of a class name added by the syntax highlighter (e.g., `class*='language-'` or a class from Prism.js/highlight.js like `.token`). For example: `const codeBlock = page.locator('pre > code').first(); await expect(codeBlock).toHaveClass(/language-.*/);`.
tasks.testStrategy: The test should pass if code blocks are found and have the expected CSS classes for styling. If the syntax highlighter fails to process the code, the test should fail.

tasks.title: Implement Getting Started Page Test
tasks.description: Create a specific test for the 'Getting Started' page to ensure its unique content, such as the initial setup steps, is visible.
tasks.details: This test will navigate directly to the 'Getting Started' page or click the corresponding link. Use `authenticatedPage.goto('/pi-controller/documentation/getting-started')`. It should then look for a unique element on that page, for instance, a heading `h3` with the text 'Installation' or 'Configuration'. `await expect(page.locator('h3:has-text("Installation")')).toBeVisible();`.
tasks.testStrategy: The test passes if it successfully navigates to the 'Getting Started' page and finds the specified unique content. It should fail if the navigation fails or the content is missing.

tasks.title: Implement Use Case Cards Test
tasks.description: Verify that the 'Use Case' cards are displayed correctly and are interactive (e.g., clickable).
tasks.details: Locate the container for the use case cards. Use a selector like `div[data-testid='use-case-cards']`. Assert that the container is visible. Then, count the number of cards within it to ensure the expected number is displayed: `await expect(page.locator('[data-testid="use-case-card"]')).toHaveCount(expectedCount);`. Finally, test that the first card is clickable and navigates to the correct URL.
tasks.testStrategy: The test should pass if the correct number of cards are rendered. It should fail if the count is wrong. Test the navigation by clicking one card and asserting the URL changes.

tasks.title: Implement 'Hide from navigation' Checkbox Test
tasks.description: Test the functionality of the 'Hide from navigation' checkbox for a documentation section, ensuring it correctly removes the item from the navigation menu.
tasks.details: This is a state-changing test. It requires identifying a specific documentation section that can be edited. Steps: 1. Navigate to the documentation index. Confirm an item, e.g., 'Troubleshooting', is visible in the nav. 2. Navigate to the edit page for 'Troubleshooting'. 3. Locate and check the 'Hide from navigation' checkbox: `page.locator('input[name="hideFromNav"]').check()`. 4. Click the 'Save' button and wait for navigation/confirmation. 5. Navigate back to the documentation index. 6. Assert that the 'Troubleshooting' link is now hidden from the navigation menu: `await expect(page.locator('nav a:has-text("Troubleshooting")')).toBeHidden();`. Add a `test.afterEach` hook to uncheck the box and restore the state.
tasks.testStrategy: This test passes if the navigation item is successfully hidden after checking the box and saving, and then reappears after it is unchecked in a cleanup step. The test requires careful state management to avoid polluting other tests.

tasks.title: Implement API Reference Page Test
tasks.description: Create a test to verify the content of the API Reference page, such as checking for the presence of endpoint definitions.
tasks.details: This test should navigate to the API Reference section. It should then check for common elements of API documentation, for instance, a rendered OpenAPI/Swagger UI component by looking for a specific data-testid or class like `.swagger-ui`. Alternatively, check for specific endpoint text, e.g., `await expect(page.locator('code:has-text("GET /api/v1/status")')).toBeVisible();`.
tasks.testStrategy: The test succeeds if the API Reference page loads and key components of the API documentation are rendered. The test should fail if the API documentation component is missing or fails to load.

tasks.title: Refactor and Organize Documentation Tests
tasks.description: Organize all created tests into logical groups using `test.describe` and add comments to improve readability and maintainability of the `documentation.spec.ts` file.
tasks.details: Review all tests in `documentation.spec.ts`. Group related tests using nested `test.describe` blocks, for example: 'Navigation', 'Page Content', 'Admin Functionality'. Add comments explaining complex assertions or test setups. Ensure consistent use of locators and patterns across all tests in the file. This task improves long-term health of the test suite.
tasks.testStrategy: A peer review of the `documentation.spec.ts` file will be conducted to ensure clarity, good organization, and adherence to project conventions. The test suite should still pass all tests after refactoring.

tasks.title: Create Error Handling Test Suite File
tasks.description: Set up the initial structure for the error handling tests by creating the `error-handling.spec.ts` file. This file will house all tests related to API errors, network failures, and incorrect route handling.
tasks.details: Create a new test file at `tests/e2e/error-handling.spec.ts`. Import `test` and `expect` from `@playwright/test`. Add a `test.describe('Error Handling Scenarios', () => { ... });` block to group all related tests. This task is foundational for implementing specific error condition tests.
tasks.testStrategy: Verify the file `tests/e2e/error-handling.spec.ts` is created in the repository. Run the test suite with no tests to ensure it's picked up by the Playwright runner without errors.

tasks.title: Implement 404 Not Found Page Test
tasks.description: Create a Playwright test to verify that navigating to a non-existent URL correctly displays the custom 404 Not Found page, as per the PRD.
tasks.details: In `error-handling.spec.ts`, add a test case: `test('should display 404 page for invalid routes', async ({ page }) => { ... });`. Navigate to a deliberately incorrect route like `/pi-controller/this-page-does-not-exist`. Use `expect(page.locator('h1')).toContainText('404');` to assert the page title. Also, verify a link/button back to the home page exists: `await expect(page.locator('a:has-text("Go Home")')).toBeVisible();`.
tasks.testStrategy: Run the Playwright test. The test should pass by successfully navigating to a non-existent page and finding the specified 404 headline and home link.

tasks.title: Implement Server Error Response Tests (500, 503)
tasks.description: Test the application's ability to gracefully handle 500 Internal Server Error and 503 Service Unavailable responses from the API.
tasks.details: In `error-handling.spec.ts`, create two tests within a `test.describe('API Server Errors')`. Use `page.route('**/api/v1/**', route => route.fulfill({ status: 500, json: { message: 'Internal Server Error' } }));` to mock a 500 error. Repeat for a 503 error. In both tests, navigate to a page that makes an API call and assert that a user-friendly error message is displayed, e.g., `await expect(page.locator('.error-message')).toContainText('Something went wrong');`.
tasks.testStrategy: Execute the tests. They should pass if the UI displays the correct error message when the API mock returns 500 and 503 status codes respectively.

tasks.title: Implement API Timeout Handling Test
tasks.description: Verify the application displays a proper error state and a retry mechanism when an API request times out, following the example in the PRD.
tasks.details: In `error-handling.spec.ts`, implement the test as specified in the PRD. Use an authenticated page fixture if necessary. Use `page.route('**/api/v1/nodes', route => { setTimeout(() => route.abort('timeout'), 5000); });` to simulate a long-running request that eventually fails. Navigate to the relevant page (`/pi-controller/nodes`) and assert the visibility of the error message and the retry button: `await expect(page.locator('.error-message')).toBeVisible();` and `await expect(page.locator('button:has-text("Retry")')).toBeVisible();`.
tasks.testStrategy: Run the test. It should mock the API timeout, and the assertions for the error message and retry button visibility must pass.

tasks.title: Implement Authorization Error Tests (401, 403)
tasks.description: Test the application's response to 401 Unauthorized and 403 Forbidden API errors, ensuring proper redirection or error display.
tasks.details: In `error-handling.spec.ts`, create two tests. For 401, mock an API endpoint with `route.fulfill({ status: 401 })`. After the action, assert the user is redirected to the login page: `await expect(page).toHaveURL('/login');`. For 403, mock the API with `route.fulfill({ status: 403 })` and assert that a 'Forbidden' or 'Access Denied' message is shown on the current page.
tasks.testStrategy: Run the tests. The 401 test should confirm redirection to the login page. The 403 test should confirm a specific 'access denied' UI element becomes visible.

tasks.title: Create Edge Cases Test Suite File
tasks.description: Set up the `edge-cases.spec.ts` file to house tests for UI states like loading, empty data, form validation, and handling of invalid data formats.
tasks.details: Create a new test file at `tests/e2e/edge-cases.spec.ts`. Import `test` and `expect` from `@playwright/test`. Add a `test.describe('UI Edge Cases', () => { ... });` block to serve as a container for the subsequent edge case tests.
tasks.testStrategy: Verify the file `tests/e2e/edge-cases.spec.ts` is created. Running the empty test suite should not produce any errors.

tasks.title: Implement Loading States Test
tasks.description: Verify that loading indicators, such as skeletons or spinners, are displayed while data is being fetched from the API.
tasks.details: In `edge-cases.spec.ts`, create a test that mocks a delayed API response. Use `page.route('**/api/v1/**', async route => { /* Assert loading state is visible */ await new Promise(f => setTimeout(f, 1000)); route.fulfill({ status: 200, json: { data: [] } }); });`. Before the `fulfill` call, assert that the loading indicator is visible, e.g., `await expect(page.locator('.spinner')).toBeVisible();` or `await expect(page.locator('.skeleton-loader')).toBeVisible();`. Then, after fulfillment, assert it is no longer visible.
tasks.testStrategy: The test should intercept a network request, confirm the loading UI is present during the artificial delay, and then confirm it disappears after the request is completed.

tasks.title: Implement Form Validation Messages Test
tasks.description: Test that form fields display appropriate validation messages when a user enters invalid data or leaves required fields empty.
tasks.details: In `edge-cases.spec.ts`, identify a form in the application. Write a test that navigates to the form, fills in some fields with invalid data (e.g., 'invalid-email' for an email field), and leaves required fields blank. Click the submit button. Assert that specific error messages appear next to the invalid fields, for example `await expect(page.locator('#email-field + .validation-error')).toContainText('Please enter a valid email');`.
tasks.testStrategy: The test will pass if, after attempting to submit an invalid form, the correct validation error messages are rendered in the DOM adjacent to their respective form fields.

tasks.title: Implement Empty States Test
tasks.description: Verify that pages or components display a user-friendly 'empty state' message when the API returns an empty list of data.
tasks.details: In `edge-cases.spec.ts`, write a test for a page that displays a list of items (e.g., nodes). Mock the corresponding API endpoint to return an empty array: `page.route('**/api/v1/nodes', route => route.fulfill({ status: 200, json: { data: [] } }));`. Navigate to the page and assert that the list container is hidden or empty, and an 'empty state' element is visible, e.g., `await expect(page.locator('.empty-state-message')).toContainText('No nodes found');`.
tasks.testStrategy: Run the test. It should pass if the application correctly renders the empty state UI instead of a blank table or list when the mocked API response is an empty array.

tasks.title: Implement Invalid API Data Handling Test
tasks.description: Test the application's resilience when an API returns a successful (200) response but with malformed or unexpected data, such as null values for required fields.
tasks.details: In `edge-cases.spec.ts`, mock an API response with a valid status code but invalid data structure. For example: `route.fulfill({ status: 200, json: { data: [{ id: 1, name: null }] } })` where the name is expected to be a string. The test should verify that the application doesn't crash and either omits the malformed item or displays a placeholder/error for that specific item without breaking the entire page.
tasks.testStrategy: The test passes if the page renders without a JavaScript crash (e.g., 'Cannot read properties of null'). Assert that the rest of the page remains functional and that the problematic data is handled gracefully.

tasks.title: Setup Accessibility Test Suite and Install Axe-Core
tasks.description: Create the new accessibility test file and install the necessary dependencies for automated accessibility auditing using axe-core with Playwright.
tasks.details:
Create a new test file at `tests/accessibility.spec.ts`. Install the `@axe-core/playwright` package, which is the official library for integrating the axe accessibility testing engine with Playwright. 

Command to run: `npm install -D @axe-core/playwright axe-core`

The test file should import `test` and `expect` from `@playwright/test` and the `AxeBuilder` from `@axe-core/playwright`. Include a basic test block to ensure the file is correctly configured.
tasks.testStrategy: Verify that the `accessibility.spec.ts` file is created in the `tests/` directory. Check `package.json` to confirm that `@axe-core/playwright` and `axe-core` are listed as devDependencies. Run the initial empty test suite to ensure it's picked up by the Playwright runner without errors.

tasks.title: Implement Automated Accessibility Audit with Axe-Core
tasks.description: Integrate and run an automated accessibility audit using axe-core on key pages of the application, such as the main dashboard and settings page, to catch common WCAG violations.
tasks.testStrategy: Run the Playwright test. The test should pass if no accessibility violations are detected by axe-core. Intentionally introduce a simple accessibility error (e.g., an image without an alt tag) and verify that the test fails with a descriptive error message from axe.

tasks.title: Test ARIA Attributes for Interactive Elements
tasks.description: Verify that all interactive elements like buttons, links, and custom controls have appropriate ARIA labels or descriptive text content to ensure they are understandable to screen reader users.
tasks.details: Create a test that locates all `button`, `a[href]`, and elements with `role='button'` or `role='link'`. For each element, assert that it has either a non-empty `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby` attribute, or meaningful `textContent`. This ensures that screen readers can announce the purpose of each control.
tasks.testStrategy: The test will iterate through all interactive elements on a given page. It should assert that each element's accessible name is not null or empty. Use Playwright locators to find the elements and `getAttribute()` or `textContent()` to check their values. The test passes if all elements meet the criteria.

tasks.title: Implement Form Label Association Test
tasks.description: Ensure all form input, select, and textarea elements have correctly associated labels. This is critical for screen reader users to understand what data is expected in each field.
tasks.details: Write a Playwright test that finds all `input`, `select`, and `textarea` elements that are not of type `hidden` or `submit`. For each element, verify that there is a corresponding `<label>` tag. The association can be checked in two ways: 1) The `for` attribute of the label matches the `id` of the input. 2) The input element is a descendant of the label element.
tasks.testStrategy: Run the test against a page containing forms, like the settings page. The test should query for all form controls and their associated labels. Use assertions to check for the presence and correctness of the `for`/`id` link or the nesting structure. The test passes if every form control has a valid associated label.

tasks.title: Verify Descriptive Text for Buttons
tasks.description: Confirm that all buttons have clear and descriptive text that accurately conveys their function, avoiding ambiguous labels like 'Click Here' or 'Submit'.
tasks.details: This test extends the ARIA attribute test (ID 174). It specifically targets `button` elements and elements with `role='button'`. The test logic should check that the accessible name (from `aria-label` or `textContent`) is descriptive and not from a predefined list of generic terms (e.g., 'Go', 'Details', 'Click').
tasks.testStrategy: Create a helper function that evaluates the accessible name of a button against a blacklist of non-descriptive terms. The Playwright test will iterate through all buttons on the page and use this helper to assert their text is meaningful. The test passes if no buttons use generic, uninformative labels.

tasks.title: Implement Keyboard Navigation and Tab Order Test
tasks.description: Verify that users can navigate through all interactive elements on the page in a logical order using the 'Tab' key for forward navigation and 'Shift+Tab' for reverse navigation.
tasks.details: Write a test that identifies all focusable elements on the page in their expected tab order. The test will start by focusing on the `body` or the first element, then repeatedly press 'Tab' and check that `page.locator(':focus')` returns the next expected element in the sequence. Implement a similar check for 'Shift+Tab'. The sequence of focusable elements can be defined in an array for comparison.
tasks.testStrategy: Execute the test on a page with a clear interaction flow, like a form or a dashboard. The test passes if the actual focus order after each 'Tab' and 'Shift+Tab' press matches the predefined expected order of elements.

tasks.title: Test Keyboard Interaction for Dialogs and Forms
tasks.description: Ensure that standard keyboard interactions work as expected: the 'Escape' key should close modal dialogs, and the 'Enter' key should submit forms when an input field is focused.
tasks.details: Create two separate test cases. For the first, trigger a modal dialog to open, then press the 'Escape' key using `page.keyboard.press('Escape')` and assert that the dialog is no longer visible. For the second, focus an input field within a form, press 'Enter' using `page.keyboard.press('Enter')`, and assert that the form submission behavior (e.g., a network request, a redirect, or a success message) is triggered.
tasks.testStrategy: The tests will be verified by checking the state of the UI after the key press. For the dialog test, assert `expect(dialogLocator).toBeHidden()`. For the form submission test, use `page.waitForNavigation()` or `page.waitForResponse()` to confirm the submission occurred.

tasks.title: Validate ARIA-Live Regions for Dynamic Status Indicators
tasks.description: Test that dynamic content updates, such as status messages or notifications, are properly announced by screen readers using `aria-live` regions.
tasks.details: Identify elements intended to be status indicators. Write a test that triggers an action causing the indicator to update (e.g., saving settings). After the action, check that the indicator element has the `aria-live` attribute set to 'polite' or 'assertive'. Then, assert that the text content of the region has been updated with the expected status message.
tasks.testStrategy: The test simulates a user action and then inspects the DOM. It will locate the `aria-live` region and use `getAttribute('aria-live')` to confirm its presence. It will then use `expect(locator).toHaveText()` to verify that the correct message appears within the region. The test passes if the attribute exists and the text is updated correctly.

tasks.title: Implement Screen Reader Page Title and Heading Hierarchy Tests
tasks.description: Verify that each page has a unique and descriptive `<title>` and that headings (`<h1>` through `<h6>`) are used in a logical, hierarchical order to facilitate screen reader navigation.
tasks.details: Create a test for page titles by navigating to multiple pages and using `expect(page).toHaveTitle()` with a descriptive regular expression or string. For heading hierarchy, create another test that fetches all heading elements (`h1, h2, h3, etc.`) in DOM order. The test logic should then verify: 1) There is exactly one `<h1>`. 2) Heading levels are not skipped (e.g., an `<h3>` does not directly follow an `<h1>`).
tasks.testStrategy: For page titles, the test passes if each page's title matches the expected value. For the heading test, the test passes if the collected list of heading levels follows a logical sequence (e.g., `[1, 2, 2, 3, 2, 3, 3]`) without out-of-order levels.

tasks.title: Refactor and Finalize Accessibility Test Suite
tasks.description: Consolidate all accessibility tests into the `accessibility.spec.ts` file, refactor any duplicated code into helper functions or `beforeEach` hooks, and ensure the entire suite runs reliably.
tasks.details: Review all implemented accessibility tests. Move common setup, such as page navigation or authentication steps, into a `test.beforeEach` block. If there are recurring actions or assertions, extract them into reusable helper functions. Ensure all tests are correctly organized within the test file and add comments where necessary to explain complex logic.
tasks.testStrategy: Run the entire `accessibility.spec.ts` file from the command line using `npx playwright test tests/accessibility.spec.ts`. The task is complete when all tests in the file pass consistently without any flaky behavior or errors.

tasks.title: Setup Performance Test Suite File
tasks.description: Create the initial test file `performance/performance.spec.ts` and set up the basic structure for running performance tests using Playwright.
tasks.details: Create a new file at `performance/performance.spec.ts`. Import `test` and `expect` from `@playwright/test`. Create a `test.describe` block for 'Performance Tests' to group all related tests. Ensure the existing `authenticatedPage` fixture can be used, as specified in the PRD dependencies.
tasks.testStrategy: Run the empty test file with the Playwright test runner (`npx playwright test performance/performance.spec.ts`) to ensure it's discovered and runs without errors. Confirm that it integrates with the existing test infrastructure.

tasks.title: Implement Initial Page Load Time Test
tasks.description: Create a test to measure the initial page load time of the dashboard, ensuring it loads in under 3 seconds.
tasks.details: Within `performance.spec.ts`, add a new test case titled 'should load dashboard in under 3 seconds'. Use `Date.now()` before and after the navigation to calculate the total load time. The navigation should use `authenticatedPage.goto('/pi-controller')` and wait for the `networkidle` state to ensure all resources are loaded. The assertion will be `expect(loadTime).toBeLessThan(3000);`.
tasks.testStrategy: Execute the test and verify that it passes on a staging or test environment. Manually verify the load time in browser developer tools to cross-reference the automated test result. Check that the test fails if the threshold is artificially lowered (e.g., to 10ms).

tasks.title: Implement Largest Contentful Paint (LCP) Test
tasks.description: Add a test to measure the Largest Contentful Paint (LCP) Core Web Vital, ensuring it is below the recommended 2.5 seconds.
tasks.details: Implement the test 'should meet LCP threshold'. Use the `page.evaluate()` method to inject a script that creates a `PerformanceObserver` to listen for `largest-contentful-paint` entries. Return the `renderTime` or `loadTime` of the LCP entry. The test will assert `expect(lcpTime).toBeLessThan(2500);`. The observer script should be wrapped in a Promise that resolves when the LCP entry is observed.
tasks.testStrategy: Run the test against the target page. Use the Lighthouse report in Chrome DevTools to verify that the LCP value reported by the test is accurate. Ensure the test correctly fails if the threshold is breached.

tasks.title: Implement Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS) and Interaction to Next Paint (INP) Tests
tasks.description: Enhance Core Web Vitals testing by adding tests for Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS) and Interaction to Next Paint (INP) to ensure a stable and responsive user experience.
tasks.details: Add two new tests. For CLS, use a `PerformanceObserver` inside `page.evaluate` to listen for `layout-shift` entries and sum their `value` property. Assert `expect(clsScore).toBeLessThan(0.1);`. For INP, the test needs to trigger an interaction (e.g., `page.click('button')`) and use a `PerformanceObserver` listening for `event` and `interaction` types to measure the duration. Assert `expect(inpDuration).toBeLessThan(200);`. Libraries like `web-vitals` can simplify gathering these metrics within `page.evaluate`.
tasks.testStrategy: For CLS, run the test and visually inspect the page for layout shifts during load. Use the browser's performance profiler to confirm CLS scores. For INP, verify the test correctly identifies the interaction and that the measured duration is plausible. Test on a component known to have slow interactions.

tasks.title: Implement Animation Smoothness Test
tasks.description: Create a test to verify that key animations on the page maintain a consistent 60 frames per second (fps).
tasks.details: This test will use Playwright's tracing capabilities. The test steps are: 1. `await browser.startTracing(page, { path: 'trace.json', screenshots: true });` 2. Trigger an animation (e.g., opening a menu, transitioning a chart). 3. `await browser.stopTracing();`. The primary validation will be manual inspection of the `trace.json` file in a trace viewer like Perfetto or Chrome DevTools to check the 'Frames' timeline for dropped frames. Programmatic validation is complex, so the initial implementation will rely on trace generation for manual review.
tasks.testStrategy: Run the test to generate the trace file. Open the trace file in `https://ui.perfetto.dev/` or Chrome DevTools (`F12 > Performance > Load profile`). Inspect the 'Frames' track and ensure a consistent green bar at 60fps during the animation, with no red dropped frames.

tasks.title: Implement Memory Leak Detection Test
tasks.description: Develop a test to detect potential memory leaks by repeatedly interacting with components and measuring JavaScript heap size.
tasks.details: The test will follow a specific pattern: 1. Navigate to the page and get baseline memory: `const initialMemory = (await page.metrics()).JSHeapUsedSize;`. 2. Loop 10-20 times: open a modal/component, perform an action, then close it. 3. Force garbage collection using a CDP session: `const session = await page.context().newCDPSession(page); await session.send('HeapProfiler.collectGarbage');`. 4. Get final memory: `const finalMemory = (await page.metrics()).JSHeapUsedSize;`. 5. Assert that `finalMemory` is not significantly larger than `initialMemory` (allowing for a small tolerance).
tasks.testStrategy: Run the test and monitor the console output for memory usage. The test should pass on a component known to be stable. Introduce a deliberate memory leak (e.g., by adding an event listener in a loop without removing it) to ensure the test fails as expected.

tasks.title: Implement Efficient Re-render Test
tasks.description: Create a test to ensure that user interactions trigger efficient component re-renders without excessive processing time.
tasks.details: This test will measure the time between a user action and the expected DOM update. Use the Performance API: 1. `page.evaluate(() => performance.mark('start-update'));`. 2. Trigger an action, e.g., `page.click('#update-button');`. 3. `await page.waitForSelector('#expected-result');`. 4. `page.evaluate(() => performance.mark('end-update'));`. 5. `page.evaluate(() => performance.measure('update-duration', 'start-update', 'end-update'));`. 6. Retrieve the measurement and assert it's below a defined threshold (e.g., 100ms).
tasks.testStrategy: Run the test against a specific interactive component. Verify that the duration measured is reasonable. Use the React Profiler (if applicable) manually to see if the component re-renders unnecessarily, and confirm that the automated test reflects inefficient updates with a higher duration.

tasks.title: Configure and Integrate Lighthouse CI
tasks.description: Set up Lighthouse CI to automatically run performance audits against pull requests, preventing performance regressions from being merged.
tasks.details: 1. Add Lighthouse CI packages: `npm install -D @lhci/cli @lhci/server`. 2. Create a configuration file `lighthouserc.json` in the project root. Configure it to run against the staging/preview URL, and set performance budgets/assertions. Example assertion: `'assert': { 'preset': 'lighthouse:recommended', 'assertions': { 'core-web-vitals': ['warn', { 'lcp': 2500 } ] } }`. 3. Create a new GitHub Actions workflow file `.github/workflows/lighthouse-ci.yml` that triggers on pull requests. The workflow will install dependencies, build the project, deploy to a preview environment (if applicable), and run `lhci autorun`.
tasks.testStrategy: Create a pull request and verify that the Lighthouse CI check runs automatically. Check the output of the action to see the Lighthouse report. Make a change that negatively impacts performance (e.g., add a large, unoptimized image) and verify that the CI check fails due to the budget assertion.

tasks.title: Configure SonarScanner in Project Repository
tasks.description: Set up the necessary local configuration file (`sonar-project.properties`) to allow the SonarQube scanner to analyze the 'pi-controller' project.
tasks.details:
Create a `sonar-project.properties` file in the root directory of the `/Users/spenceryork/Projects/pi-controller` repository. This file will define essential project parameters for SonarQube. Assuming the project is a Node.js application, configure properties for the project key, source code location, test file locations, and test execution report paths. Example configuration:

# Unique project key
sonar.projectKey=pi-controller
# Project display name
sonar.projectName=Pi Controller

# Source code location
sonar.sources=src
# Test file location
sonar.tests=src
# Include test files in coverage analysis
sonar.test.inclusions=**/*.test.js,**/*.spec.js

# Language
sonar.language=js
# Encoding
sonar.sourceEncoding=UTF-8

# Path to test coverage report (assuming Jest is used)
sonar.javascript.lcov.reportPaths=coverage/lcov.info
tasks.testStrategy: Run `sonar-scanner` locally with a dry run or preview option (`-Dsonar.analysis.mode=preview`) to ensure the configuration is read correctly and the scanner can find the source and test files without errors. The command should execute successfully.

tasks.title: Perform Initial Baseline SonarQube Scan and Generate Report
tasks.description: Execute the first full SonarQube scan on the main branch of the codebase to establish a baseline for code quality, security vulnerabilities, and test coverage.
tasks.details: Navigate to the project root directory and execute the SonarScanner command, ensuring the `SONAR_TOKEN` environment variable is set with a valid token from the SonarQube server. Command: `cd /Users/spenceryork/Projects/pi-controller && sonar-scanner -Dsonar.login=$SONAR_TOKEN`. After the scan completes, access the SonarQube dashboard, locate the 'pi-controller' project, and export the list of all identified issues. This report will be the foundation for the remediation plan.
tasks.testStrategy: Verify that a new project named 'Pi Controller' appears in the SonarQube dashboard. Check that the dashboard is populated with metrics for bugs, vulnerabilities, code smells, coverage, and duplications. Confirm the lines of code analyzed seem correct for the project size.

tasks.title: Integrate SonarQube Scan into GitHub Actions CI Workflow
tasks.description: Create a GitHub Actions workflow to automatically run the SonarQube scanner on every push to the main branch and on every pull request.
tasks.details:
Create a new workflow file at `.github/workflows/sonarqube.yml`. Use the official `sonarsource/sonarqube-scan-action@master`. The workflow should checkout the code, set up the appropriate runtime (e.g., Node.js), run tests with coverage, and then execute the SonarQube scan. Store `SONAR_TOKEN` and `SONAR_HOST_URL` as GitHub Secrets. 

Example YAML snippet:
```yaml
name: SonarQube Scan
on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened]
jobs:
  sonarqube:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v3
    - name: SonarQube Scan
      uses: sonarsource/sonarqube-scan-action@master
      env:
        SONAR_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SONAR_TOKEN }}
        SONAR_HOST_URL: ${{ secrets.SONAR_HOST_URL }}
```
tasks.testStrategy: Create a test pull request. Verify that the 'SonarQube Scan' action triggers and completes successfully. Check the SonarQube dashboard to see the PR-specific analysis.

tasks.title: Remediate All Blocker and Critical Bugs
tasks.description: Analyze the initial SonarQube report, identify all issues categorized as 'Blocker' or 'Critical' bugs, and implement fixes.
tasks.details: Filter the issues in the SonarQube dashboard by Severity (Blocker, Critical) and Type (Bug). Create a remediation plan, starting with the highest severity. Common issues to address include Null Pointer Exceptions (add null checks), Resource Leaks (use `finally` blocks or try-with-resources constructs), and unhandled exceptions. For each fix, ensure existing tests pass and add a new unit test that specifically covers the bug scenario to prevent regressions.
tasks.testStrategy: After committing and pushing fixes, run a new SonarQube scan. Verify in the SonarQube dashboard that the count of Blocker and Critical bugs has been reduced to zero.

tasks.title: Remediate All Blocker and Critical Security Vulnerabilities
tasks.description: Identify and fix all 'Blocker' or 'Critical' security vulnerabilities reported by SonarQube to achieve a Security Rating of 'A'.
tasks.details: Filter the SonarQube report for Security Vulnerabilities with Blocker or Critical severity. Focus on common web vulnerabilities if applicable, such as SQL Injection (use parameterized queries/prepared statements with a library like `pg` or `mysql2`), Cross-Site Scripting (XSS, use context-aware output encoding libraries like `he`), and insecure dependencies (run `npm audit fix` or `yarn audit` and update `package.json`).
tasks.testStrategy: Re-scan the project after implementing fixes. Confirm in the SonarQube dashboard that the resolved security vulnerabilities are no longer reported and the overall Security Rating for the project is 'A'.

tasks.title: Increase Test Coverage to > 80%
tasks.description: Write new unit and integration tests for untested code paths to meet the project goal of greater than 80% test coverage.
tasks.details: Use the coverage report from SonarQube (or generated locally by a tool like Jest) to identify files and code branches with low coverage. Prioritize writing tests for critical business logic and complex functions. For a Node.js project using Jest, run `npx jest --coverage` to generate a local report. Add new `*.test.js` or `*.spec.js` files with tests that cover previously untested logic.
tasks.testStrategy: After adding new tests, run a new SonarQube scan. Verify that the 'Coverage' metric on the SonarQube dashboard for the project exceeds 80%.

tasks.title: Refactor Major Code Smells and Reduce Code Duplication
tasks.description: Address major code smells and refactor duplicated code blocks to improve maintainability and achieve a rating of 'A' or 'B', with less than 3% duplication.
tasks.details: Analyze the SonarQube report for Code Smells and Duplication. Prioritize 'Major' code smells and large duplicated code blocks. For duplicated code, extract the logic into reusable functions or classes. For smells like overly complex or long functions, apply the Single Responsibility Principle to break them into smaller, more focused units. Replace magic numbers with named constants.
tasks.testStrategy: Run a new SonarQube scan after refactoring. Verify that the Maintainability Rating is 'A' or 'B' and the Duplicated Lines percentage is below 3%. Ensure all existing tests pass after refactoring.

tasks.title: Configure and Activate SonarQube Quality Gate
tasks.description: Implement the official 'Pi-Controller Quality Gate' in the SonarQube server settings based on the criteria defined in the PRD.
tasks.details:
Navigate to the 'Quality Gates' section in the SonarQube administration panel. Create a new quality gate named 'Pi-Controller Quality Gate'. Add conditions based on the PRD's JSON specification, focusing on metrics for 'on New Code'.
1. `new_coverage` < `80`
2. `new_duplicated_lines_density` > `3`
3. `new_maintainability_rating` is worse than `A` (op: GT, error: 1)
4. `new_reliability_rating` is worse than `A` (op: GT, error: 1)
5. `new_security_rating` is worse than `A` (op: GT, error: 1)
Finally, associate this quality gate with the 'pi-controller' project.
tasks.testStrategy: After configuring the quality gate, review a recent analysis on the main branch. Verify that the project dashboard shows a 'Passed' status for the new quality gate. Intentionally create a PR with a failing condition (e.g., low coverage) to test that it correctly shows a 'Failed' status.

tasks.title: Enforce Quality Gate in GitHub Actions for PRs
tasks.description: Update the GitHub Actions workflow to check the Quality Gate status after a scan and fail the CI check if it does not pass, effectively blocking merging of non-compliant PRs.
tasks.details:
Modify the `.github/workflows/sonarqube.yml` workflow. Add a step that uses the `sonarsource/sonarqube-quality-gate-action@master` action. This step will poll SonarQube for the analysis result and fail if the Quality Gate status is 'FAILED'. Ensure this action runs only on pull request triggers. Set a timeout to prevent waiting indefinitely.

Example addition:
```yaml
    - name: SonarQube Quality Gate check
      uses: sonarsource/sonarqube-quality-gate-action@master
      timeout-minutes: 5
      env:
        SONAR_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SONAR_TOKEN }}
```
tasks.testStrategy: Create a new pull request that violates one of the quality gate conditions (e.g., introduces duplicated code). Verify that the GitHub Actions workflow runs, the 'SonarQube Quality Gate check' step fails, and a red 'X' appears next to the commit, blocking the merge.

tasks.title: Document New Coding Standards and Quality Gate Requirements
tasks.description: Create or update project documentation to reflect the new code quality standards, quality gate rules, and common patterns to avoid.
tasks.details: In the project's `CONTRIBUTING.md` or a new `CODING_STANDARDS.md` file, document the key requirements of the Quality Gate (80% coverage on new code, no new critical issues, etc.). Add a section with examples of common issues found during the initial remediation (e.g., 'How to avoid race conditions in our code') and the preferred solutions. If any major refactorings led to architectural changes, create or update an Architecture Decision Record (ADR).
tasks.testStrategy: Review the created documentation with the development team to ensure it is clear, accurate, and provides actionable guidance. Verify that a link to the new standards is included in the project's main README.md.

tasks.title: Setup TaskMaster Environment and Validate CLI
tasks.description: Initialize the project for TaskMaster by installing the necessary tools, creating the required directory structure, and ensuring all Product Requirements Documents (PRDs) are correctly placed.
tasks.details: Install the `task-master` command-line tool globally or as a project dependency. Create the `.taskmaster/docs/` directory in the project root. Copy all 13 PRD `.txt` files into this new directory. Verify the installation by running `task-master --version`. This initial setup is critical for all subsequent parsing and management tasks.
tasks.testStrategy: Run `task-master --version` and ensure it returns a version number. List the contents of the `.taskmaster/docs/` directory to confirm all 13 PRD files are present. The script should exit with a status code of 0 if successful.

tasks.title: Parse All PRDs into TaskMaster
tasks.description: Execute the TaskMaster CLI commands to parse all PRDs into a single, consolidated `tasks.json` file. This involves running an initial parse command followed by a series of append commands for the remaining PRDs.
tasks.details: Using a shell script, first run `task-master parse-prd .taskmaster/docs/prd-01-setup-infrastructure.txt`. Following that, loop through the remaining 12 PRDs (from `prd-02` to `prd-13`) and execute `task-master parse-prd .taskmaster/docs/[prd-file] --append` for each. This will create a unified `.taskmaster/tasks/tasks.json` file.
tasks.testStrategy: Verify that the file `.taskmaster/tasks/tasks.json` is created. Open the JSON file and check that it contains a non-empty array of task objects. Confirm that the total number of top-level tasks corresponds to the content of all parsed PRDs (the PRD mentions 16 tasks should be generated).

tasks.title: Analyze Task Complexity and Expand Subtasks
tasks.description: Use TaskMaster's analysis and expansion features to enrich the generated tasks. This step involves analyzing complexity, automatically breaking down complex tasks into smaller subtasks, and validating the resulting dependency graph.
tasks.details: Execute the following commands in sequence: `task-master analyze-complexity --research`, `task-master expand --all --research`, and `task-master validate-dependencies`. The `--research` flag suggests an AI-driven analysis, so the output should be reviewed for correctness. The final step generates markdown files for each task, which should also be inspected.
tasks.testStrategy: Review the complexity analysis report generated by the CLI. Inspect the `tasks.json` file to confirm that tasks marked as complex now contain a `subtasks` array. Run `task-master validate-dependencies` and ensure it completes without errors, indicating a logical dependency graph. Check for the presence of generated markdown files in the `.taskmaster/tasks/` directory.

tasks.title: Define Agent Roles and Configuration
tasks.description: Create a structured JSON configuration file that defines the roles and responsibilities of each agent type (Test, Remediation, Quality, Documentation) as specified in the PRD.
tasks.details: Create a new file at `.taskmaster/agents.json`. In this file, define a JSON object with keys for each agent role. Each role object should specify its name, a description of its responsibilities, and the types of tasks it's assigned to (e.g., using tags or ID ranges). Example: `{"roles": [{"name": "Test Agent", "description": "Executes Playwright tests...", "task_pattern": "^2\..*"}]}`. This file will be used for automated task assignment.
tasks.testStrategy: Validate the `.taskmaster/agents.json` file against a JSON schema to ensure its structure is correct. Write a simple script to read and parse the file, printing the defined roles to the console to verify its contents are accessible.

tasks.title: Implement Agent State Management Service
tasks.description: Develop a centralized Node.js module to manage the state of all tasks and agents. This service will handle reading from and writing to a shared status file, ensuring data integrity during parallel agent operations.
tasks.details: Create a module, e.g., `src/taskmaster/stateService.js`. This module will manage a central state file, e.g., `.taskmaster/state.json`. Use a file-locking library like `proper-lockfile` (latest version) to prevent race conditions. The service should expose functions like `getTaskStatus(taskId)`, `updateTaskProgress(agentUpdatePayload)`, and `getDashboardView()`. The payload for updates should match the JSON structure specified in the PRD's 'Agent Communication' section.
tasks.testStrategy: Create unit tests for the `stateService.js` module. Test concurrent write attempts to ensure the file lock works as expected. Verify that `updateTaskProgress` correctly updates the state file and that `getTaskStatus` retrieves the correct information.

tasks.title: Develop Agent Task Assignment and Execution Script
tasks.description: Create a master script that agents can run to receive their next assigned task based on their role and the defined parallel execution tracks. The script will use the `task-master` CLI to manage task status.
tasks.details: Create a Node.js script, e.g., `scripts/run-agent.js`, that accepts an agent role as an argument (e.g., `node scripts/run-agent.js --role=TestAgent1`). The script will: 1. Read `.taskmaster/tasks.json` and `.taskmaster/state.json`. 2. Determine the next available task for that role based on the PRD's execution tracks, dependencies, and current status. 3. Use `child_process.exec` to run `task-master next --role=[role]` (assuming the CLI can be extended or filtered) or implement the logic manually. 4. Once a task is assigned, run `task-master set-status --id=[id] --status=in-progress`. The agent's specific logic (e.g., running a test) would then execute.
tasks.testStrategy: Run the script for different roles. Verify that it correctly identifies and assigns the first task in each track (e.g., Task 1.1 for a setup agent, Task 2.1 for Test Agent 1). Check the `state.json` file or use `task-master list` to confirm the task's status is updated to 'in-progress'.

tasks.title: Implement Agent Progress Reporting Protocol
tasks.description: Create a standardized method for agents to report their progress, results, and any issues encountered during task execution. This will interact with the State Management Service.
tasks.details: Create a client module, e.g., `src/taskmaster/agentClient.js`, that agents will use to communicate. This module will have a primary function, `reportProgress(updateObject)`, which takes a JavaScript object matching the PRD's communication JSON format. This function will call the `stateService.updateTaskProgress()` method to persist the update. This decouples the agent's core logic from the state management implementation.
tasks.testStrategy: Write a mock agent script that imports `agentClient.js`. The script should perform a fake task and call `reportProgress` with sample data (e.g., progress: 0.50, tests_passed: 5). Verify that the `.taskmaster/state.json` file is correctly updated with this detailed information.

tasks.title: Develop Web-based Monitoring Dashboard
tasks.description: Create a simple web-based dashboard to visualize the progress of tasks, the status of agents, and overall project completion based on the data in the central state file.
tasks.details: Since the project uses Express.js, add a new route, e.g., `/dashboard/taskmaster`, to the existing Express app. This route's handler will read the consolidated data from `stateService.getDashboardView()`. The data will be passed to a simple EJS or Pug template. On the frontend, use a library like Chart.js (v4.x) to render visualizations for 'Track completion percentage' and 'Test pass/fail rates'. The dashboard should auto-refresh every 30 seconds by fetching data from an API endpoint.
tasks.testStrategy: Start the web server and navigate to the `/dashboard/taskmaster` URL. Verify that the dashboard loads and accurately reflects the current data in `.taskmaster/state.json`. Manually update the state file and refresh the dashboard to ensure it displays the new information correctly. Test that charts render properly.

tasks.title: Simulate and Test Parallel Agent Execution
tasks.description: Test the entire workflow by simulating the execution of multiple agents working in parallel on different tracks. This will validate the task assignment, state management, and reporting mechanisms under concurrent load.
tasks.details: Create a test script (e.g., using `npm-run-all` or `concurrently`) that launches multiple instances of the `scripts/run-agent.js` script with different roles (e.g., `TestAgent1`, `TestAgent2`). The mock agents should perform their tasks, report progress, and complete. This test will ensure that the file locking in the State Service prevents data corruption and that tasks are assigned and updated correctly.
tasks.testStrategy: Run the parallel execution script. Monitor the `.taskmaster/state.json` file and the web dashboard during the test. Verify that tasks in different tracks move from 'pending' to 'in-progress' to 'done' correctly. Ensure there are no errors related to file access or data corruption. Confirm the final state reflects the successful completion of all simulated tasks.

tasks.title: Create Workflow Documentation
tasks.description: Produce comprehensive documentation covering the TaskMaster setup, agent workflow, progress tracking, and troubleshooting, as required by the PRD.
tasks.details: Create a new directory `/docs/taskmaster`. Inside, create the following markdown files: 1. `setup_guide.md`: Details how to install the CLI and initialize the project. 2. `agent_workflows.md`: Describes the agent roles, the task assignment logic, and the parallel execution tracks. 3. `progress_tracking.md`: Explains how to use the dashboard and interpret the data. 4. `dependency_diagram.md`: Include a Mermaid.js chart showing the task dependency graph. 5. `troubleshooting.md`: Lists common issues and their solutions.
tasks.testStrategy: Have a team member follow the documentation to set up the project from scratch. They should be able to initialize TaskMaster, run a mock agent, and view the dashboard successfully. Review the documents for clarity, accuracy, and completeness against the PRD requirements.
